coverage.note: Written by the authoring session, asserted by scripts/verify_strengths_personality_library.js. If these numbers disagree with the blends object the tests fail. Never edit by hand.

note: Facilitator-only teaching library, third of the planned set. Sits alongside library-strengths-gifts.json and library-personality-gifts.json and never replaces either. Rows are the 34 CliftonStrengths themes; columns are the 72 unique 16Personalities strength descriptors, the same deduplicated set used by library-personality-gifts.json. 34 x 72 = 2448 cells. Where both axes name the same underlying trait the cell is an amplification card naming the doubled instinct and the missing counterweight, rather than pretending the pair is a contrast. Never import this file into the page; it is served only by api/library.js after authentication.

Analytical|Altruistic.recognize: You will give anyone your time, but you want to know the need is genuine first, so you ask questions others would find cold. The care is real and the checking protects it. What you never run the same scrutiny over is your own supply.
Analytical|Altruistic.ask: When did you last hold your own reserves to the standard you hold a request to?

Analytical|Analytical.recognize: You do not accept a conclusion until you have taken it apart and found the shape underneath, and you are usually right. But there is no second voice in the room to tell you when the taking-apart is finished. The work stays open long after the answer arrived.
Analytical|Analytical.ask: What would have to be true for you to call this settled today?

Analytical|Bold.recognize: You will take a real risk, but only one you have already run the numbers on, which makes you look braver than you feel. Others see the leap and not the hours behind it. People then follow you into risks they have not thought through, assuming you did that part for them.
Analytical|Bold.ask: Who is copying your decisions without doing your homework?

Analytical|Calm and Practical.recognize: You stay visibly unrattled, and you reduce a crisis to its working parts while others are still reacting. That is why people bring you the mess. But your steadiness reads as agreement, and by the time you state a concern the room has moved on assuming you had none.
Analytical|Calm and Practical.ask: What have you decided against that nobody around you knows you decided against?

Analytical|Charismatic.recognize: You draw people in before you have said anything substantive, and then you back it up with something rigorous, which is rare. The risk is that the first thing lands harder than the second. You get believed for the wrong reason and let it stand, because correcting it slows things down.
Analytical|Charismatic.ask: When were you last agreed with by someone who had not understood you?

Analytical|Charming.recognize: You loosen people up and then ask the hard question, and it lands because they never saw it coming. That works. It also means people are unsure which mode they are in with you, and some learn to stay guarded rather than be caught out twice.
Analytical|Charming.ask: Who has stopped being open with you, and do you know why?

Analytical|Clear Communication.recognize: You can take something you have examined in detail and say it in one sentence anybody can use. That is genuinely rare. The cost is that the sentence travels without the work behind it, and when challenged you end up defending a summary rather than what you actually think.
Analytical|Clear Communication.ask: What is the fuller version of that, and who has heard it?

Analytical|Creative.recognize: You make things, and then you take your own work apart before anyone else can. The result is better than most first drafts ever get. But that taking-apart has no natural stopping point, and some of what you have made is finished and sitting unshown.
Analytical|Creative.ask: What is done that you are still calling unfinished?

Analytical|Curious.recognize: You follow a question until it opens, then check whether the opening holds. Most people do one or the other. What it costs is time. The checking makes every path longer, so you go deep on three things in a month when the work in front of you needed six.
Analytical|Curious.ask: What did you not get to this month because something else was more interesting?

Analytical|Decisive Action.recognize: You decide fast, but only because you worked the options in the background where nobody watched. It looks like instinct. The danger is that you start trusting the speed itself, and one day you will move at the same pace on something you never actually examined.
Analytical|Decisive Action.ask: Which of your recent quick calls did you not really work through first?

Analytical|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with something long past the point others quit, and you keep checking whether staying is still right, which is why it usually is. But sometimes the honest answer arrives and you overrule it, because leaving would mean an earlier judgment of yours was wrong.
Analytical|Dedicated.ask: What are you still committed to that your own reasoning already released you from?

Analytical|Determined.recognize: You drive through resistance and can explain exactly why the resistance is mistaken. That combination is hard to argue with. It is also hard to interrupt. People who disagree stop trying, and you read the quiet that follows as having persuaded them.
Analytical|Determined.ask: Who stopped arguing with you, and how would you tell the difference?

Analytical|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You see the small wrong thing and can show why it matters, which prevents real damage more often than anyone credits. But you find more than any team can act on, and when it all arrives at the same weight the important item is buried in the list.
Analytical|Diligent and Observant.ask: Of everything you flagged last week, which one actually mattered most?

Analytical|Direct.recognize: You say what you have concluded, plainly, and you have usually earned the conclusion. People know where you stand. What they do not get is the working. You present the verdict, so anyone who might have improved it never sees where to push.
Analytical|Direct.ask: When did you last show someone the reasoning instead of the answer?

Analytical|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You tell people what you actually think, including about yourself, and it is examined rather than raw. That makes you trustworthy in a way few are. It also means your self-criticism arrives fully evidenced, and nobody can talk you out of it.
Analytical|Direct and Authentic.ask: Whose assessment of you would you accept over your own?

Analytical|Direct and Honest.recognize: You offer the difficult information before anyone asks, and you have already checked it, so it holds up under pressure. The problem is timing rather than content. You deliver when your case is complete, not when the person is ready, and completeness is your clock.
Analytical|Direct and Honest.ask: Who needed that from you a week earlier than they got it?

Analytical|Disciplined.recognize: You hold a standard and can defend every part of it, which is why yours survives pressure that collapses other people's. But a standard built from evidence still ages, and yours is protected by an argument you made years ago and have not reopened since.
Analytical|Disciplined.ask: Which of your rules have you never re-examined?

Analytical|Easygoing.recognize: You are unbothered by most things and precise about the few that matter, so people underestimate how much you have already thought about. That works in your favour until it does not. The calm reads as no opinion, and decisions get made without asking you.
Analytical|Easygoing.ask: What got decided recently that you had a view on and did not give?

Analytical|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You find the wasted step and demonstrate that it is wasted, so nobody can defend it. Systems get faster around you. The risk is that some steps carried something you did not measure, like reassurance or a quiet check, and those vanish without leaving a mark.
Analytical|Efficient Organizer.ask: What disappeared along with the step you took out?

Analytical|Empathetic.recognize: You pick up what a person is carrying and then look for what caused it, which means your help often lasts rather than soothing for an hour. But you can treat a person as something to be understood, and being understood correctly is not the same as being met.
Analytical|Empathetic.ask: When did someone last want your company rather than your explanation?

Analytical|Energetic.recognize: You bring drive and you aim it at the right thing, because you checked the target before you moved. That pairing is rare. But your pace is set by how sure you are, and when you are sure you assume everyone else is too, so nobody gets room to catch up.
Analytical|Energetic.ask: Who is still working through what you already settled?

Analytical|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You put things in order and can justify every category, so the system survives after you leave the room. The cost is that ordering something feels like progress. You will spend a day building the structure when the work itself needed four hours.
Analytical|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: What did you organise this week instead of doing?

Analytical|Enthusiastic.recognize: You have already vetted whatever you back, so your excitement carries real weight and people move on it fast. That is exactly why you should be careful. Your warmth gets treated as your conclusion, and you are rarely as certain as you sound.
Analytical|Enthusiastic.ask: How sure are you, actually, about the thing you sold hardest this month?

Analytical|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You can produce many options and then kill most of them yourself, which is the part most people cannot do. But you kill them privately, so the group only ever sees survivors and never learns what you weighed. Eventually they stop bringing their own.
Analytical|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: When did you last let someone else eliminate one of your ideas?

Analytical|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You explain a complicated thing so well that people believe they now understand it, and often they do. But your fluency outruns their grasp by about a day. They nod in the room and cannot reproduce it later, and you find out only when the work comes back wrong.
Analytical|Excellent Communicators.ask: Who agreed with you and then could not repeat it back?

Analytical|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You build a system and can show why each part earns its place, so people trust it and use it. The trouble is that you keep improving it. Everyone else learned version one, and the version you are running is three ahead of theirs.
Analytical|Excellent Organizers.ask: What are you still refining that other people already consider finished?

Analytical|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You read a room accurately and then check your read against what people actually do, so you are seldom fooled. That makes you effective and slightly unnerving. Some people sense they are being assessed even while you are being warm, and they never fully relax around you.
Analytical|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who behaves differently when you walk in, and what does that tell you?

Analytical|Future Focused.recognize: You see where a thing is heading and you can show your working, which is why people take your warnings seriously. But being right early is not the same as being useful early. You raise it while the evidence is thin to everyone else, and get dismissed once.
Analytical|Future Focused.ask: What did you call correctly that nobody acted on, and what would make the next one land?

Analytical|Generous.recognize: You give freely, and you give to the thing you have determined will actually work, so your giving does more than most. What you do not examine with the same care is the total. Each decision is sound and the sum of them is more than you have.
Analytical|Generous.ask: If you added up everything you have committed to, would the number surprise you?

Analytical|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You can make the thing and explain why it is built that way, so what you make holds up and can be repaired by someone else. But you keep finding one more improvement, and the difference between finished and nearly finished has stopped being visible to you.
Analytical|Good Practical Skills.ask: What would happen if you handed it over exactly as it is right now?

Analytical|Good at Connecting with Other.recognize: You connect people only when you can see the fit, so your matches land where most people's waste everyone's time. The cost is volume. You hold back dozens of connections that would have worked, because you could not see in advance exactly how.
Analytical|Good at Connecting with Other.ask: Who did you decide not to connect because the fit was not obvious enough?

Analytical|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You lift a room and you do not lie to do it, because you only say the encouraging thing you can actually support. People come to rely on that. But when you have nothing supportable to say you go quiet, and your silence has become the loudest signal you send.
Analytical|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: What does the room conclude when you say nothing?

Analytical|Grounded.recognize: You do not move when pushed, and you can name exactly what you are standing on, which makes you the anchor in a wobbly group. But the same firmness applies to positions you formed with less information than you have now, and you do not revisit those on your own.
Analytical|Grounded.ask: What do you still hold that you first decided with less than you know today?

Analytical|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You would rather touch the thing than read about it, and you notice what the report left out. That is why your assessments are trusted. But you form them from the piece in your hands, and you rarely go back to ask whether that piece was typical.
Analytical|Hands-on and Observant.ask: How do you know the one you looked at was representative?

Analytical|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You get things working with whatever is available, and you understand exactly why your fix works, which is why it usually lasts. That is also the problem. It lasts long enough that nobody funds the real repair, and you are the only one who knows it is temporary.
Analytical|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What is still running on something you meant to replace?

Analytical|Hardworking.recognize: You work hard and you work on the right thing, because you check before you start. That combination produces a lot. But your measure of enough is whether the question is fully answered, and questions do not close on a schedule, so nothing tells you to stop.
Analytical|Hardworking.ask: What would tell you today's work is done, other than running out of hours?

Analytical|Honest.recognize: You own your errors and you can explain precisely how they happened, which is why people forgive them quickly. But your account is so complete that it can sound like a defence. The person you wronged wanted an apology and received a diagnosis.
Analytical|Honest.ask: When did you last say you were sorry without explaining why it happened?

Analytical|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state the position and the evidence in the same breath, so nobody wastes time guessing where you are. It is efficient and it is fair. What it is not is gentle, and some people hear a case being made against them when you were only showing your work.
Analytical|Honest and Direct.ask: Who thinks you were arguing with them when you were thinking out loud?

Analytical|Idealistic.recognize: You want the better version and you can specify exactly what it would take, which turns a vague hope into a plan other people can join. The cost is private. You measure everything that exists against something you have fully worked out, and it always falls short.
Analytical|Idealistic.ask: What is good enough right now that you have not let yourself call good?

Analytical|Imaginative.recognize: You imagine something and then immediately look for what would break it, so what survives is worth building. But the survival rate is low and nobody sees the ones that did not make it, so you are known as practical by people who have no idea how much you invent.
Analytical|Imaginative.ask: What have you never said out loud because you killed it first?

Analytical|Independent.recognize: You work things out yourself and you can show why your conclusion holds, so you do not need the room to agree with you. That is real strength. It also means you check with nobody, and a flaw in your reasoning can travel a long way before it meets resistance.
Analytical|Independent.ask: Who is allowed to tell you that you got something wrong?

Analytical|Informed.recognize: You know what is going on and you know which parts of it are reliable, which is rarer than being merely well read. But you pass on the full picture with its qualifications intact, and people who wanted a decision receive a briefing instead.
Analytical|Informed.ask: What is your actual recommendation, in one sentence, with the caveats removed?

Analytical|Insightful.recognize: You reach the centre of a problem quickly and then go back and verify the route, so your insight survives scrutiny. The gap is in the telling. People experience the arrival and not the verification, so your best thinking sounds like a guess that happened to work.
Analytical|Insightful.ask: When did you last walk someone through how you got there?

Analytical|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: Your encouragement means something because you only give it when it is deserved, and everybody around you knows that. But it means the absence of it is information too, and people who are struggling read your silence as a verdict you never actually delivered.
Analytical|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who is waiting to hear something from you that you assumed they already knew?

Analytical|Knowledgeable.recognize: You hold a great deal and you hold it accurately, having checked most of it yourself. That makes you the person people ask. It also makes you the person who cannot let a small error pass, and the fix costs more relationship than the error ever cost anyone.
Analytical|Knowledgeable.ask: Which correction this week was worth what it cost you?

Analytical|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You commit after you have looked hard at what you are committing to, so your commitments hold when other people's break. The trouble is that the looking happened once. Circumstances have changed since, and your loyalty is running on an assessment nobody has updated.
Analytical|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: If you were deciding this today, from scratch, would you choose the same?

Analytical|Observant.recognize: You see what is actually happening rather than what is being said about it, and you confirm before you conclude. That makes you nearly impossible to mislead. But confirming takes time, and by the time you are certain the moment to say something has closed.
Analytical|Observant.ask: What did you see clearly and never mention?

Analytical|Open-Minded.recognize: You will consider anything, and you hold it up against what you can verify, so you change your mind for good reasons rather than for the last person who spoke. But the willingness reads as no position at all, and people stop asking what you think.
Analytical|Open-Minded.ask: What do you actually believe here, before anyone else has spoken?

Analytical|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have a way of working and you can defend every part of it, so your output is steady where other people's swings. But the way of working was designed for the job you had then. You keep meeting the current job with a shape you validated long ago.
Analytical|Organized and Effective.ask: What in your routine is there because it works, and what is there because it always has been?

Analytical|Original.recognize: You do not take the standard approach, and you can articulate exactly what is wrong with it, so your departures are principled rather than merely oppositional. But you have been right often enough that disagreeing has become comfortable, and comfort is not a reason.
Analytical|Original.ask: When did you last land on the conventional answer and keep it?

Analytical|Passionate.recognize: You care with your whole self about a small number of things, and you have checked that each one deserves it. That is why your conviction moves people who ignore louder voices. But the checking happened at the start, and nothing since has been allowed to reopen it.
Analytical|Passionate.ask: What would it take for you to step back from this, and has any of it happened?

Analytical|Perceptive.recognize: You notice what people are not saying and then look for something that confirms it, which keeps you from inventing stories about them. The cost is that you often confirm it privately and act on it without ever asking, so the person never gets to correct you.
Analytical|Perceptive.ask: Which of your reads has the person themselves never heard?

Analytical|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You keep a group moving and you do it with things you can actually stand behind, so morale around you is not fragile. But you hold the difficult finding until you are completely sure of it, and by then the group has built plans on the version you did not correct.
Analytical|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: What are you sitting on until you are certain, and what is being built on it meanwhile?

Analytical|Principled.recognize: Your convictions are reasoned rather than inherited, which means you can explain them and they hold up. It also means you expect other people's to be reasoned too, and when someone believes something for reasons they cannot articulate, you hear it as no belief at all.
Analytical|Principled.ask: Whose conviction have you dismissed because they could not defend it the way you would?

Analytical|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You start before you are asked, and you start on the right thing because you looked first. Work gets ahead of schedule around you. But you looked alone, and the thing you determined was needed is sometimes a thing somebody else had already decided against.
Analytical|Proactive Initiative.ask: What did you get well ahead on before anyone confirmed it was wanted?

Analytical|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You answer fast and the answer usually holds, because the examination happened in the background rather than not at all. The risk sits in how it looks. People take your quickness as permission to skip their own thinking, and copy the conclusion without the process.
Analytical|Quick Thinkers.ask: Who is relying on your first answer as though it were your final one?

Analytical|Rational.recognize: You weigh everything and wave nothing through, because the same instinct is running here twice and the two reinforce rather than balance each other. You are almost never wrong on the substance. What has no counterweight is anything that cannot be argued.
Analytical|Rational.ask: What do you know is true that you could not defend in an argument?

Analytical|Rational and Practical.recognize: You take a problem apart until it becomes a task somebody can do, and you check the task actually addresses the problem. Few people do both halves. But some things people bring you are not problems at all, and you have already begun breaking them down before you notice.
Analytical|Rational and Practical.ask: Who came to you this month wanting to be heard rather than helped?

Analytical|Receptive.recognize: You take in what people bring you and weigh it honestly instead of defending your position, which is why people keep bringing you things. But weighing is not the same as answering, and some of what you took in is still sitting with you, unanswered, months later.
Analytical|Receptive.ask: Who is still waiting on a response from you?

Analytical|Reliable.recognize: You do what you said, and you only said it after working out whether you could, so your word is worth more than most people's. What you never examine on the same terms is the accumulation. Every promise was sound alone; together they exceed the week.
Analytical|Reliable.ask: Which commitment would you drop first if you had to drop one today?

Analytical|Research-Oriented.recognize: You are the most dependable source in any room and also the last one ready, because the same instinct is doubled here and doubling it does not sharpen, it delays. The decision that needed a good answer on Tuesday is still waiting for a better one on Friday.
Analytical|Research-Oriented.ask: What decision is waiting on you right now, and what is the cost of the delay?

Analytical|Results Oriented.recognize: You complete things and you check that what you completed was worth completing, which is why your delivered work rarely gets thrown away. But the check happens at the start and the end, and in between you will spend whatever it takes, including people.
Analytical|Results Oriented.ask: Who paid for the last thing you delivered on time?

Analytical|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You care about people and you are careful not to comfort them with something untrue, which is why your reassurance holds when other people's evaporates. But you deliver the hard part first because it is the accurate part, and the kindness that arrives second sometimes arrives too late.
Analytical|Sensitive and Warm.ask: What did you say accurately this week that you wish you had said gently?

Analytical|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You notice how something will land and you change tack, and you check afterwards whether the change worked. That is real skill. But you also move your position and not just your delivery, and the thing you actually concluded gets quietly filed away unspoken.
Analytical|Sensitive to Others.ask: What conclusion of yours has nobody ever heard, because of how it would land?

Analytical|Sociable.recognize: You enjoy people and you form real judgments about them rather than collecting names, so you know who is who in a way most sociable people do not. The cost is that you are always partly assessing, and there are few rooms where you are simply present.
Analytical|Sociable.ask: Where do you go where you are not evaluating anything?

Analytical|Spontaneous.recognize: You move on an opening quickly, but only on openings you have already thought about at some point, so what looks like a whim has years behind it. Nobody can see that. To the people around you, you are unpredictable, and they plan for a version of you that does not exist.
Analytical|Spontaneous.ask: Who has been surprised by you when you were not being sudden at all?

Analytical|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You can do the thing and you understand why it works, so you fix problems other people can only escalate. That makes you the one everything routes to. Nobody has asked whether that is a good use of you, and you have not raised it either.
Analytical|Strong Practical Skills.ask: Who never learned this because you were always available?

Analytical|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take responsibility seriously and you work out precisely what you owe, so you meet duties other people let slide. But you calculate each debt and never the total load, and the sum of things you genuinely owe has quietly become more than one person can carry.
Analytical|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: What do you owe that nobody would actually hold you to?

Analytical|Strong-willed.recognize: You hold your ground and you have the reasoning to back it, which means pressure alone does not move you and should not. The failure mode is narrow but real. New information and pressure often arrive together, and you dismiss both because the second one is present.
Analytical|Strong-willed.ask: When was the last time you changed position under pressure, and what did it take?

Analytical|Supportive.recognize: You support people, and you support them in ways you have thought through, so what you offer actually helps rather than just feeling kind. But you assess whether someone is ready before you support them, and some people have never been offered your help because they failed a standard they never saw.
Analytical|Supportive.ask: Who did you decide was not ready, and did you ever tell them?

Analytical|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with people and you can say exactly why they are worth it, which makes your loyalty feel like a judgment rather than a habit. That is its strength and its trap. Once you have made the case, questioning the person would mean questioning your own case.
Analytical|Very Loyal.ask: What would someone have to do for you to reconsider, and would you notice if they did it?

Analytical|Very Responsible.recognize: You trace a failure honestly when it happens, including back to yourself, and you do not flinch at what you find. That is why you are trusted with real problems. But your tracing keeps arriving at your own door, and at some point the finding stopped being a fact and became an expectation.
Analytical|Very Responsible.ask: What went wrong recently that genuinely was not yours?

Context|Altruistic.recognize: You help people, and you know the whole story of how they got here, so what you offer fits the person rather than the category. But you carry every history you have been told, and nobody has ever asked what it costs to hold that many.
Context|Altruistic.ask: Whose story are you carrying that you were never meant to keep?

Context|Analytical.recognize: You go back to how something started and take apart what happened, so you explain the present better than anyone in the room. The risk is that a full account of the past feels like an answer for the future, and it is not one.
Context|Analytical.ask: What would you do next, if the history had turned out to be different?

Context|Bold.recognize: You take risks other people call reckless, but you have checked how this went the last three times, so you are gambling less than it appears. What you cannot see is the case with no precedent, and those are the ones where your courage arrives without its usual guardrail.
Context|Bold.ask: When did you last commit to something with nothing behind it to go on?

Context|Calm and Practical.recognize: You are not shaken by a crisis because you have seen its ancestors, and you say so, which steadies everyone around you. But some things really are new, and your first instinct is to file them next to something familiar rather than look at them fresh.
Context|Calm and Practical.ask: What is happening right now that has no precedent you can point to?

Context|Charismatic.recognize: You draw people in and then give them the story behind the thing, which is why they stay rather than drift off after the first impression. But the story is one you have told many times, and the version you tell now is smoother than what actually happened.
Context|Charismatic.ask: Which part of the story have you polished until it stopped being true?

Context|Charming.recognize: You settle people by knowing where they came from, and it works because the interest is real. The cost is one-sided. You know a great deal about most people in your life, and rather fewer of them know much about you.
Context|Charming.ask: Who knows your history as well as you know theirs?

Context|Clear Communication.recognize: You can give someone the background in three sentences and they finally understand why things are the way they are. That is a real service. But three sentences is your version of the story, and yours has decided already which parts mattered.
Context|Clear Communication.ask: Who else was there, and would they tell it the same way?

Context|Creative.recognize: You ground what you make in something real, so it has weight that invented work lacks. But you build every new thing out of material you already have, and there are forms you will never reach because nothing in your past resembles them.
Context|Creative.ask: What would you make if you were not allowed to reference anything?

Context|Curious.recognize: Your questions go backwards rather than sideways, and you keep asking until you reach the beginning, which is why you understand things other people only use. But the beginning is always further back, and you will follow it past the point where anyone still needs the answer.
Context|Curious.ask: How far back do you actually need to go to decide this?

Context|Decisive Action.recognize: You decide firmly, and the decision is informed by how this has played out before, which is why your calls hold up. But precedent is your evidence, and when precedent is thin you still decide at the same speed and with the same certainty.
Context|Decisive Action.ask: Which recent decision had nothing behind it and got made like it did?

Context|Dedicated.recognize: You remain because you remember what it took to get here, and that memory keeps you in things other people abandon early. It also keeps you in things that ended a while ago, because leaving would mean the cost you paid bought nothing.
Context|Dedicated.ask: What are you still paying for that already gave you everything it was going to?

Context|Determined.recognize: You press forward carrying the whole story of why it matters, and that story is what gets you through the parts where other people stop. But it also makes retreat feel like betrayal, so you keep going on things where stopping would cost you nothing but pride.
Context|Determined.ask: What would you have to admit about the past in order to stop this now?

Context|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You spot the small thing because you remember how it looked before, and that comparison is invisible to everyone else. It makes you the early warning system. But you also flag deviations that are simply change, and people cannot always tell which kind you have brought them.
Context|Diligent and Observant.ask: Is this actually a problem, or is it just different from how it used to be?

Context|Direct.recognize: You say the hard thing and you can name when it started, which is harder to dismiss than an opinion. But bringing the history into a disagreement changes what it is. The other person came to discuss today and is now defending three years of themselves.
Context|Direct.ask: When did you last raise something without mentioning the last time it happened?

Context|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You tell people who you actually are by telling them where you came from, and that kind of honesty builds trust fast. But you offer it early and in full, and some people are not ready to receive that much of someone they just met.
Context|Direct and Authentic.ask: Who did you tell too much, too soon?

Context|Direct and Honest.recognize: You offer the uncomfortable background before anyone asks, which stops bad decisions being made from a clean slate that never existed. The trouble is that the background often implicates somebody still in the room, and you deliver it as fact rather than as an accusation you have not admitted to making.
Context|Direct and Honest.ask: Who was the last person to hear their own history repeated back to them by you?

Context|Disciplined.recognize: You keep the standard and you know why the standard exists, which is why yours does not erode the way rules with forgotten reasons do. But the reason and the rule have fused for you, and questioning the rule sounds to you like denying what happened.
Context|Disciplined.ask: If the original reason disappeared tomorrow, would you drop the rule?

Context|Easygoing.recognize: You are bothered by very little, partly because you have watched most things resolve themselves before. That perspective calms other people down. It also means you sometimes reassure them out of memory rather than attention, and you were not actually looking at this one.
Context|Easygoing.ask: What did you tell someone would be fine without really checking?

Context|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You cut waste without cutting the things that are there for a reason, because you know which is which. That makes your cuts survive where other people's has to be undone. But you also defend steps whose reason expired, and you defend them with a story.
Context|Efficient Organizer.ask: Which of these are we keeping because it works, and which because of what happened once?

Context|Empathetic.recognize: You feel what someone is going through and you know what led them there, so you rarely misread anyone. The weight is the problem. You hold the whole history alongside the feeling, and you cannot set either down when the conversation ends.
Context|Empathetic.ask: What are you still carrying from a conversation that finished months ago?

Context|Energetic.recognize: Your drive comes from somewhere specific rather than from temperament, and that makes it durable in a way pure enthusiasm is not. But it is fuelled by something that already happened, and when the memory dims you have no other source and no idea why the energy went.
Context|Energetic.ask: What is driving you now that is not about something from before?

Context|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You put things in order according to how they came to be, which produces a system that makes sense to anyone who knows the story. The problem is everyone else. Newcomers face an order whose logic lives entirely in your head.
Context|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: Could someone who arrived last month find anything without asking you?

Context|Enthusiastic.recognize: You get people excited by telling them where a thing came from, and it lands harder than a pitch about the future because it is true. But your enthusiasm needs the whole story to work, and sometimes people just needed the short version and a decision.
Context|Enthusiastic.ask: What could you have asked for this week without explaining any of the background?

Context|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You turn out a lot of options and each one is anchored to something that actually worked somewhere, so your lists are usable rather than fantasy. The limitation is invisible. Everything you produce is a variation on something that exists, and you will not notice the shape that is missing.
Context|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: Which idea on your list has no ancestor at all?

Context|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You tell it well and you tell it whole, so people understand not just what is happening but why. That is why you get asked to explain things. But the whole version takes as long as it takes, and some rooms needed four minutes and got twenty.
Context|Excellent Communicators.ask: What could you have left out and still been understood?

Context|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You build systems that account for how things actually went wrong before, so yours survive contact with reality. The cost is accumulation. Every past failure has left a safeguard behind, and the system is now carrying protections against problems that no longer exist.
Context|Excellent Organizers.ask: Which safeguard is protecting you from something that cannot happen anymore?

Context|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You connect with people by remembering their details, and they feel known rather than handled, because they are. But you also remember how they behaved under pressure two years ago, and you are relating to that person alongside the one in front of you.
Context|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who have you not let become different?

Context|Future Focused.recognize: You predict what is coming by knowing what came before, which makes your forecasts far more reliable than most. But every forecast you make is the past extended forward, so the genuine break is the one thing your method cannot see coming.
Context|Future Focused.ask: What would have to change for your read on this to be completely wrong?

Context|Generous.recognize: You give to people and causes you have watched over time, so your giving goes where it does real good rather than where the appeal was loudest. But you keep giving to the ones you have always given to, and new need has to displace old loyalty to reach you.
Context|Generous.ask: When did you last give to something you had no history with?

Context|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You make things the way they were made to last, because you learned from something that lasted. What you make holds. But you also work the way you were taught, and you have not seriously looked at whether the newer method is better or just unfamiliar.
Context|Good Practical Skills.ask: What have you dismissed as a shortcut without ever trying it?

Context|Good at Connecting with Others.recognize: You bring people together with the story of who they are, so the connection starts warm rather than transactional. But you keep everyone you have ever met, and the network you maintain takes hours nobody sees and gives back less than it used to.
Context|Good at Connecting with Others.ask: Which relationships are you maintaining out of obligation to who they used to be?

Context|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You lift people by reminding them they have survived worse, and coming from you it is not empty because you were there. But not everything is survivable by comparison, and some griefs get waved past with a reference to an older one.
Context|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: What have you compared to something else instead of just letting it be hard?

Context|Grounded.recognize: You are steady because you know where you stand and how you came to stand there, and that makes you nearly impossible to unsettle. It also makes you slow to move, because moving means leaving ground you can account for and stepping onto ground you cannot.
Context|Grounded.ask: What are you refusing to try because you cannot yet explain it?

Context|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You work with the thing in front of you and you know what it looked like last time, so you spot the change instantly. But your attention is split between the object and the memory, and occasionally you are correcting toward a state that was never actually better.
Context|Hands-on and Observant.ask: Are you fixing this, or restoring it to how it used to be?

Context|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You solve it with what is available because you remember solving something similar with less. That resourcefulness gets people out of trouble repeatedly. It also means you reach for the remembered fix before you look at whether this problem is actually the same one.
Context|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What did you fix quickly that you never went back and looked at properly?

Context|Hardworking.recognize: You work hard and you know exactly what the work is for, because you were there when it started. That makes the grind meaningful rather than mechanical. But the reason is historical, and you have not asked recently whether it is still the reason.
Context|Hardworking.ask: Why are you working this hard, and is that still true?

Context|Honest.recognize: You own what you did and you can place it in the sequence that led there, which makes your admissions credible rather than performative. But you also keep a full record of your own failures, and you consult it far more often than anyone else does.
Context|Honest.ask: What are you still holding against yourself that everyone else forgot?

Context|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state things plainly and you state where they came from, which means people cannot pretend a problem appeared out of nowhere. That is valuable and it is uncomfortable. Naming the origin usually names a person, and you do it without deciding first whether that serves anything.
Context|Honest and Direct.ask: Does saying where it started actually help fix it?

Context|Idealistic.recognize: You want something better and you know what better looked like, because you have seen a version of it work. That makes your hope concrete rather than naive. But the version you saw belonged to different conditions, and you are measuring today against something that had advantages nobody here has.
Context|Idealistic.ask: What made that work then, and does any of it still exist?

Context|Imaginative.recognize: Your imagining has texture because it is assembled from things you actually witnessed. It is more believable than most people's imagining and easier to build. But your imagination is furnished entirely from your own life, and its walls are exactly where your experience ends.
Context|Imaginative.ask: What can you not picture at all, and whose experience would you need to borrow?

Context|Independent.recognize: You work alone well because you carry the background yourself and do not need briefing. That makes you fast and self-sufficient. It also means the context stays with you, and the people working alongside you are operating on a fraction of what you know.
Context|Independent.ask: What do you know about this that nobody else on the team knows?

Context|Informed.recognize: You know what is going on now and how it got that way, so your read is deeper than anyone following headlines. But you cannot deliver the current state without the sequence attached, and people who asked what is happening receive how we got here.
Context|Informed.ask: Can you tell me where this stands without telling me how it started?

Context|Insightful.recognize: You see what is really going on because you know what came before, and your reads on people and situations are unusually accurate. The failure is specific. When something genuinely new appears, you reach for the closest thing you have seen and are confidently wrong.
Context|Insightful.ask: When were you sure about something and completely mistaken, and what had you matched it to?

Context|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: Your encouragement names something specific a person actually did, so it lands as recognition rather than flattery. But you encourage people toward who they have been, and someone trying to become different hears their old self being praised.
Context|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who are you praising for something they are trying to leave behind?

Context|Knowledgeable.recognize: You hold a great deal and you hold where each piece of it came from, which makes you far more reliable than someone who merely remembers facts. But you are also the keeper of what really happened, and setting the record straight has become something you do without weighing whether it matters.
Context|Knowledgeable.ask: Which correction did you make this week that changed nothing?

Context|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You remain with people because you remember what they did for you, and that kind of loyalty is rare and worth having. But debts do not expire in your accounting, and you are still repaying some to people who would not remember lending.
Context|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: Who do you feel you owe, and would they say you still do?

Context|Observant.recognize: You notice change because you have a baseline nobody else kept, and that makes you the first to know something has shifted. But you wait a while to be sure it is real, and by the time you are certain the shift has finished happening.
Context|Observant.ask: What have you been watching that you should have named a month ago?

Context|Open-Minded.recognize: You will hear a new idea out, and you place it against everything similar you have seen, so you evaluate it fairly rather than by novelty. But an idea with no comparison available gets less of your attention, not more, and those are usually the important ones.
Context|Open-Minded.ask: What idea have you set aside simply because you had nothing to compare it to?

Context|Organized and Effective.recognize: Your way of working was built out of what actually went wrong before, so it protects against real failures rather than imagined ones. But it has only ever grown. Nothing has been removed from it in years, and it now takes longer to follow than the work takes to do.
Context|Organized and Effective.ask: What step could you drop, and what are you afraid would happen?

Context|Original.recognize: You depart from the usual approach only when you know why it exists and where it came from, so your departures are informed rather than reflexive. But you are most original about things you know deeply, and everywhere else you quietly do what is done.
Context|Original.ask: Where are you following convention simply because you never learned its history?

Context|Passionate.recognize: You care about things because of something that happened, and that makes your conviction unshakeable and specific. It also makes it hard to share. People are asked to feel strongly about a thing whose weight comes from a story that is not theirs.
Context|Passionate.ask: Can you make someone care about this without telling them what it cost you?

Context|Perceptive.recognize: You size people up accurately because you have known them over time, not because you are guessing from a single interaction. That accuracy is real. But time also builds an expectation, and you sometimes see what the person has always done rather than what they are doing now.
Context|Perceptive.ask: Who surprised you recently, and had you stopped expecting them to?

Context|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You keep people going by pointing at what has been built, and it works because it is evidence rather than cheerleading. But you reach for the record whenever things get heavy, and some conversations needed you to sit in the difficulty rather than point away from it.
Context|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: When did you last let something be bad without balancing it against something good?

Context|Principled.recognize: You hold a line and you know exactly what happened to make that line necessary, which is why you hold it when it is inconvenient. But you also remember who crossed it, and your line has quietly become a ledger with names in it.
Context|Principled.ask: Who have you not forgiven, and does the principle actually require that?

Context|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You start early because you recognise the shape of what is coming from having seen it before. That head start is genuinely valuable. But you also act on the assumption it will unfold the same way, and you commit resources before anyone else agrees it is the same thing.
Context|Proactive Initiative.ask: What have you already started that nobody has agreed to yet?

Context|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You answer fast because you are matching, not calculating, and the match is usually right. That makes you look brilliant in the moment. It also means your fastest answers are your least examined ones, and they arrive with the same confidence as your best.
Context|Quick Thinkers.ask: Which of your instant answers have you never gone back and checked?

Context|Rational.recognize: You argue from what actually happened rather than from theory, which makes your positions hard to dislodge and usually correct. But you treat the record as settled fact, and the record is a set of things you remember, selected by what mattered to you at the time.
Context|Rational.ask: Who would remember that differently, and have you ever asked them?

Context|Rational and Practical.recognize: You solve the problem in front of you using what has worked before, so your solutions are proven rather than clever. That is why they stick. But you reach for the proven one first every time, and something better may exist that you have simply never had reason to try.
Context|Rational and Practical.ask: When did you last solve something in a way you had never used before?

Context|Receptive.recognize: You remember what people told you last time, and being remembered is rare enough that they keep coming back. But you take it in and you hold it, and you have become the place where a great deal of other people's difficulty is stored.

Context|Reliable.recognize: You honour your word, and you honour it because you remember what it felt like when someone did not. That gives your reliability a spine most people's lacks. But it also means breaking a commitment feels like becoming someone you once resented, so you never renegotiate one.
Context|Reliable.ask: What promise are you keeping that everyone involved would happily release you from?

Context|Research-Oriented.recognize: You check things properly, and you know which sources have been right before, so your checking is faster and better aimed than a general search. But you have decided who is credible based on a track record you built years ago and have not revisited.
Context|Research-Oriented.ask: Whose judgment have you trusted for so long that you stopped evaluating it?

Context|Results Oriented.recognize: You complete things, and you know why completing this particular thing matters, which keeps you going past the point where the task alone would not. But you defined the destination at the start, using what you knew then, and you are still driving at that definition.
Context|Results Oriented.ask: Is the finish line you are running at still the right one?

Context|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: Your care for people is specific because you know what they have been through, so you are gentle in exactly the right places. But you are also gentle about wounds that have healed, and you keep handling someone carefully long after they stopped needing it.
Context|Sensitive and Warm.ask: Who are you still protecting from something they are over?

Context|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You adapt to people accurately because you know what lands badly with each of them, and that is why you rarely cause harm by accident. But those adaptations have accumulated into a map of what not to say, and there are now subjects you avoid with people who have moved on.
Context|Sensitive to Others.ask: What can you not say to someone because of something that happened years ago?

Context|Sociable.recognize: You enjoy people and you keep track of them, so your circle has depth rather than being a list of acquaintances. The cost is arithmetic. You maintain everyone you have ever been close to, and the maintenance has begun to crowd out anyone new.
Context|Sociable.ask: When did you last make a genuinely new friend?

Context|Spontaneous.recognize: You act on the moment, but the moments you act on are ones you recognise, so your sudden moves land better than most people's. What you rarely notice is the recognition doing the work. You experience it as freedom and it is actually a very narrow gate.
Context|Spontaneous.ask: When did you last act on something you did not recognise?

Context|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You take on what comes up, and you know how the thing was built, so you fix rather than replace. That saves a great deal. But you also know why every part is the way it is, and that knowledge has made you the only person who can maintain it.
Context|Strong Practical Skills.ask: What have you never written down that would be lost tomorrow?

Context|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take on what you owe, and your sense of what you owe comes from specific things people did for you, which makes it real rather than abstract. But nothing ever leaves that ledger, and you are still carrying duties from a season of your life that ended.
Context|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: Which duty did you take on for a version of your life you are no longer living?

Context|Strong-willed.recognize: You hold firm and you can say exactly what you are holding to, which makes you very hard to move and usually right to be. But some of what you are holding to is a decision made under conditions that no longer apply, and you defend it as though it were principle.
Context|Strong-willed.ask: Is this a conviction, or a decision you made once and never reopened?

Context|Supportive.recognize: You support people in the specific way they have needed before, so your help fits rather than being generic. But you keep offering the help that was needed then, and the person in front of you may have outgrown it and be too grateful to say so.
Context|Supportive.ask: Have you asked recently what they actually need from you now?

Context|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with people through things that would end most relationships, because you remember who they were when it counted. That loyalty is a rare gift to receive. It also means you excuse behaviour you would not accept from anyone you had known a shorter time.
Context|Very Loyal.ask: What would you refuse to tolerate from a stranger that you accept from them?

Context|Very Responsible.recognize: You take the blame for what happens, and you can reconstruct exactly how it happened, so your reckoning is honest and unusually complete. But you keep every one of those reconstructions, and the collection has become a case you are building against yourself.
Context|Very Responsible.ask: If someone else had done all of that, would you judge them the way you judge you?

Futuristic|Altruistic.recognize: You give yourself to work whose payoff is years out, which is why you stay with causes that lose everyone else. But you are sustained by a picture of what this becomes, and the people working beside you are living in the part that is hard right now.
Futuristic|Altruistic.ask: Does the person next to you know what you are picturing, or are they just tired?

Futuristic|Analytical.recognize: You see where this goes and then take apart whether it holds, so what you propose survives challenge. But the taking apart happens after you are already committed to the picture, and it tends to find reasons rather than test them.
Futuristic|Analytical.ask: What would change your mind about this, and are you actually looking for it?

Futuristic|Bold.recognize: You commit to something distant and you commit hard, which is how big things ever start. The exposure is not the risk itself but the timeline. You are asking people to bear real cost now for a payoff only you can currently see.
Futuristic|Bold.ask: What is the first thing that will prove you right, and when does it arrive?

Futuristic|Calm and Practical.recognize: You describe a distant thing in a steady voice, which makes it sound achievable rather than fanciful, and that is why people follow you. But your calm also flattens urgency, and the near-term problems that would stop this get raised and absorbed rather than solved.
Futuristic|Calm and Practical.ask: What is happening this month that could end this before it starts?

Futuristic|Charismatic.recognize: You paint what could be and people want to be part of it, which is how you gather a room in an afternoon. That is also the danger. They joined the picture rather than the work, and the work is where you will need them.
Futuristic|Charismatic.ask: Who signed up for the vision and has not been told what the first year looks like?

Futuristic|Charming.recognize: You make a large ambition feel comfortable to be around, so people who would normally resist it lean in. But that comfort also lets you move past the hard question, and objections get charmed rather than answered.
Futuristic|Charming.ask: What has someone raised twice that you have never actually addressed?

Futuristic|Clear Communication.recognize: You can say where this is going in words anyone can repeat, which is why your ideas travel further than better ones. But the simple version leaves out the difficulty, and people commit to a picture they would not have chosen if they had heard the whole of it.
Futuristic|Clear Communication.ask: What did you leave out to make it sound this simple?

Futuristic|Creative.recognize: You make things that belong to a moment that has not arrived, and when it does arrive your work is already there. That is rare and valuable. In the meantime it is misunderstood, and you have to keep going with almost no confirmation.
Futuristic|Creative.ask: What are you making now that nobody will understand for a while, and can you last that long?

Futuristic|Curious.recognize: Your questions are about what could exist rather than what does, and you follow them a long way, which is where genuinely new things come from. But every answer opens another distance, and you are always further out than the thing you actually started.
Futuristic|Curious.ask: What did you begin and leave, and would it still be worth finishing?

Futuristic|Decisive Action.recognize: You see it and you sign up immediately, which is how you get a year ahead of everyone. But you decide at the moment of seeing, when the picture is at its most persuasive and least examined, and you rarely revisit that first call.
Futuristic|Decisive Action.ask: What did you sign up to on day one that you would not choose today?

Futuristic|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with something for years because you can still see the end of it, and that endurance is what long work requires. But the picture is your sustenance and nobody else has it, so you burn through people who joined for a season and were asked for a decade.
Futuristic|Dedicated.ask: Who left, and did you understand why at the time?

Futuristic|Determined.recognize: You drive toward something distant and you do not stop when it gets hard, which is the only way anything long ever gets built. But you also do not stop when the destination changes, and you can spend years driving at a version of the future that already moved.
Futuristic|Determined.ask: Is the thing you are working toward still the thing you would choose today?

Futuristic|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You notice the early signal that something is starting, which is why you are ahead so often. But you notice from a distance and you report it as significant, and most early signals amount to nothing. People have learned to discount you, including on the ones that matter.
Futuristic|Diligent and Observant.ask: How many of your early warnings actually came true, and do you know the number?

Futuristic|Direct.recognize: You say where this is heading without softening it, and you are usually right, which is exactly why it lands badly. People hear that what they are currently building has an expiry date, and you have delivered a forecast that lands as a judgment.
Futuristic|Direct.ask: How would you say that so the people doing today's work do not hear it as a dismissal?

Futuristic|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You tell people plainly what you hope for, including the parts that sound unreasonable, and that honesty is why the right people find you. But you say the full ambition early, and some hear arrogance where you meant openness.
Futuristic|Direct and Authentic.ask: Who backed away after you told them what you were really aiming at?

Futuristic|Direct and Honest.recognize: You will tell someone their current path leads nowhere, before they ask, because you can see the end of it. Sometimes that saves years. But you deliver a conclusion about their future with the same confidence you would use about the weather, and it is not the same thing.
Futuristic|Direct and Honest.ask: How certain are you, really, and did you say it that way?

Futuristic|Disciplined.recognize: You hold a long ambition and you keep the daily habits that get you there, which is the combination almost nobody manages. But the habits were designed for the version of the goal you had at the start, and you keep them even as the goal drifts.
Futuristic|Disciplined.ask: Which of your daily disciplines is still serving where you are actually headed?

Futuristic|Easygoing.recognize: You hold a big picture without being anxious about it, which makes you unusually pleasant company for someone that ambitious. But the ease means you rarely convert the picture into a next step, and years pass with the vision intact and unstarted.
Futuristic|Easygoing.ask: What is the smallest thing you could do this week toward it?

Futuristic|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You design for where this is going rather than where it is, so what you build does not need rebuilding in two years. But you also remove things the current operation still depends on, because in the version you can see they are gone.
Futuristic|Efficient Organizer.ask: What did you cut for a future that has not arrived yet?

Futuristic|Empathetic.recognize: You feel what people are going through and you can also see them past it, so you offer hope that is specific rather than hollow. But you sometimes arrive at the hope before they have finished the feeling, and being told it gets better is not always what is wanted.
Futuristic|Empathetic.ask: Who needed you to stay in it with them and got moved along instead?

Futuristic|Energetic.recognize: Your drive is fed by something years away, which means it does not depend on this week going well. That makes you durable. But it also means you set a pace against a distant clock, and the people beside you are pacing against a much nearer one.
Futuristic|Energetic.ask: Who around you is running at your speed without your reason?

Futuristic|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You set things up for the size you expect to be rather than the size you are, so you rarely have to redo it. The cost is now. The current team is carrying a structure built for a group three times its number.
Futuristic|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: What is your team maintaining that only makes sense if you grow?

Futuristic|Enthusiastic.recognize: You light people up about something that does not exist yet, and that is genuinely how things get started. But excitement has a shelf life and the timeline does not, so the gap between how it felt at the beginning and where it is now becomes its own problem.
Futuristic|Enthusiastic.ask: What did you get people excited about that has not moved since?

Futuristic|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You turn out possibilities faster than any group can process, and most of them point somewhere real. But you keep producing after the room has chosen, and the choice never gets to settle because there is always a better option arriving.
Futuristic|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: What has your team decided that you have quietly kept reopening?

Futuristic|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You describe what is coming so well that people can see it too, and that shared picture is what makes long work possible. But you can describe it far better than you can start it, and the description keeps satisfying the room in place of progress.
Futuristic|Excellent Communicators.ask: What exists so far, apart from the way you talk about it?

Futuristic|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You line up the pieces toward something years out, so what you put in place still fits when you get there. Very few plans survive that long. But you are managing today's people against a chart whose logic only makes sense from the end.
Futuristic|Excellent Organizers.ask: Does anyone else understand why this piece has to happen now?

Futuristic|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You connect with people around what they could become, and being seen that way is powerful enough that they stay close to you. But it is also a form of pressure, and some people are exhausted by being related to as a potential rather than a person.
Futuristic|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who have you never told is fine exactly as they are?

Futuristic|Future Focused.recognize: You are almost always right about direction and almost never present for what is happening now, because the same pull runs here twice with nothing to balance it. The distance is not a habit you could drop; it is where you actually live, and everyone around you knows it.
Futuristic|Future Focused.ask: What is true this week that you have not looked at?

Futuristic|Generous.recognize: You give to things whose return is distant or invisible, which is where the most needed giving usually goes. But you commit against a future capacity rather than a current one, and the generosity was pledged by someone who assumed things would be better by now.
Futuristic|Generous.ask: What did you promise from money or time you do not yet have?

Futuristic|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You make things that anticipate what will be needed rather than only what is asked, so your work ages well. But you also make things for a use case nobody has requested yet, and some of what you have made is waiting for a demand that never came.
Futuristic|Good Practical Skills.ask: What have you built that has still not been used?

Futuristic|Good at Connecting with Other.recognize: You bring people together because you can see what they might build together, not just because they should meet. Some of those pairings turn into real things. But you are matching against a possibility, and the two people involved have to live in the present where it might not work.
Futuristic|Good at Connecting with Other.ask: How many of your introductions have you followed up on?

Futuristic|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You keep a room hopeful by pointing at what is coming, and coming from you it is believable rather than empty. But it also means nothing present is ever allowed to be simply bad, and the people in a hard season keep being handed a future instead of company.
Futuristic|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: When did you last agree that something was hard without adding anything?

Futuristic|Grounded.recognize: You carry a distant ambition and a firm sense of what must not change, and that pairing is what keeps big plans from becoming fantasy. But the two are in tension inside you constantly, and people cannot predict which one they are getting on a given day.
Futuristic|Grounded.ask: Which is it here: are you moving, or holding, and does anyone else know?

Futuristic|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You work with what is in front of you while thinking about what it becomes, so your hands stay busy and your work still points somewhere. But you leave out the middle steps that connect them, and other people are left assembling a path between today and your picture.
Futuristic|Hands-on and Observant.ask: What is the step between where this is now and where you say it is going?

Futuristic|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You make do now because you are certain the proper version is coming, and that keeps things moving through lean years. But the temporary arrangement was justified by a future date, and the date has been moved several times without the arrangement being revisited.
Futuristic|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What is still temporary that you set up two years ago?

Futuristic|Hardworking.recognize: You work relentlessly because you can see what it is for, and that makes the labour bearable in a way it is not for people who cannot. But the payoff keeps receding, and you have been paying at full rate for a return that has no date on it.
Futuristic|Hardworking.ask: When is this supposed to get easier, and who told you that?

Futuristic|Honest.recognize: You own it when a direction you championed is not working, which is harder for you than most because you saw it so clearly. That honesty is worth a great deal. But you tend to say so publicly and completely, and the abrupt reversal costs people who had reorganised around you.
Futuristic|Honest.ask: Who had already committed to the thing you just dropped?

Futuristic|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state where things are heading and you do not hedge it, which lets people plan honestly instead of guessing. But an unhedged forecast is heard as a fact, and when it turns out otherwise the credibility you lose is larger than the error was.
Futuristic|Honest and Direct.ask: What did you state as certain that you were actually only fairly sure about?

Futuristic|Idealistic.recognize: You aim at something better and you can see the route, which turns hope into something with steps rather than sentiment. But nothing that arrives ever matches what you pictured, and you have a long record of achievements that felt like near misses.
Futuristic|Idealistic.ask: What have you accomplished that you have never let yourself be pleased about?

Futuristic|Imaginative.recognize: You can build an entire world in an afternoon and it will be coherent, detailed and completely unstarted, because one instinct is wearing two names here and nothing brakes it. Imagining it is so satisfying that it competes with making it.
Futuristic|Imaginative.ask: What have you imagined in such detail that making it feels redundant?

Futuristic|Independent.recognize: You pursue a distant thing without needing anyone to agree, which is often the only way an unpopular direction survives long enough to be proven. But nobody checks the picture, and a vision that has never met resistance is not the same as one that has withstood it.
Futuristic|Independent.ask: Who has genuinely argued against this, and what did they say?

Futuristic|Informed.recognize: You follow what is happening and you place it on a line heading somewhere, so your read on events is more useful than a summary. But you report the destination alongside the news, and people cannot always tell where the reporting stops and your projection starts.
Futuristic|Informed.ask: Which part of that is what happened, and which part is where you think it goes?

Futuristic|Insightful.recognize: You see what a situation is really about and where it ends up, often in the same moment, and you are right far more than chance. But the two arrive fused, and you present a conclusion about the future with the certainty that belonged to the insight about now.
Futuristic|Insightful.ask: Which part of that do you actually know, and which part are you extending?

Futuristic|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You encourage people by telling them what they could become, and for someone stuck that can be the thing that moves them. But it lands differently on someone doing their best right now, who hears that their present effort is a stage on the way to acceptable.
Futuristic|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who needs to hear that what they did this week was already enough?

Futuristic|Knowledgeable.recognize: You hold a great deal and you use it to work out where things go, which makes your predictions substantive rather than intuition. But holding more than the room makes it easy to dismiss the person who doubts you, and doubt from an uninformed person can still be right.
Futuristic|Knowledgeable.ask: Who disagreed with you that you dismissed because they did not know enough?

Futuristic|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You remain with people and projects for the length of time a distant goal actually takes, and almost nobody does. But your patience is funded by the picture, and when the picture finally fades you will leave suddenly, which will look to everyone else like it came from nowhere.
Futuristic|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: What are you still inside that you privately stopped believing in?

Futuristic|Observant.recognize: You look closely for the first signs of what you expect, which means you often see it before anyone else can. But expecting something is a poor state in which to be looking, and you will find the early evidence for your picture whether or not it is there.
Futuristic|Observant.ask: What have you seen lately that argues against where you think this is going?

Futuristic|Open-Minded.recognize: You will consider any version of what might come, so you are not trapped in a single forecast the way most long-range thinkers are. But every new possibility is genuinely interesting to you, and the direction the team is following changes more often than they can absorb.
Futuristic|Open-Minded.ask: How many times has your team heard a different plan from you this year?

Futuristic|Organized and Effective.recognize: You work against a distant target, which is why your calendar has direction instead of being a list of next actions. But that approach assumes the target holds, and you keep executing the sequence long after you privately started doubting the destination.
Futuristic|Organized and Effective.ask: If you stopped believing in the goal, how long before your calendar would show it?

Futuristic|Original.recognize: You go a different way because you can see where the standard way ends, and that is why your departures are often vindicated later. But being early and being different feel identical from the inside, and you cannot always tell which one you are doing.
Futuristic|Original.ask: Are you ahead on this, or just against it?

Futuristic|Passionate.recognize: You care intensely about something that does not exist yet, and that intensity is what carries a long project through its unrewarding middle. But nothing present can compete with it for your attention, and the people and work in front of you are quietly rationed.
Futuristic|Passionate.ask: What in your life right now gets whatever is left over?

Futuristic|Perceptive.recognize: You size a person up and see what they are heading toward, which makes your sense of people unusually forward-looking and often right. But a judgment about someone's direction is a story you made, and you act on it before they have chosen it.
Futuristic|Perceptive.ask: Have you ever told someone where you thought they were going and been wrong?

Futuristic|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You keep a group's morale up by keeping the destination visible, and in a long project that is not optional, it is the job. But you have made yourself the only source of it, and on the days you cannot hold the picture there is nothing else holding the room.
Futuristic|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: What keeps this going on a week when you have nothing?

Futuristic|Principled.recognize: You hold to a line because you can see what happens to the people who do not, several steps down the road. That gives your convictions a practical edge rather than only a moral one. But you judge others for outcomes that have not happened, and they are being held responsible for your forecast.
Futuristic|Principled.ask: Who are you thinking less of for something they have not actually done?

Futuristic|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You start on the thing that will be needed before anyone asks, and when the need arrives you are already halfway. That timing is a real advantage. But you also start on things whose need never materialises, and nobody counts those because you never announced them.
Futuristic|Proactive Initiative.ask: How much of your effort this year went to something that never got needed?

Futuristic|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You think fast and you think forward, so in a conversation you are already three moves out while everyone else is on the first. That is why you are useful in a crisis. It is also why people feel talked past, and stop offering the thing you jumped over.
Futuristic|Quick Thinkers.ask: Who stopped contributing in your meetings, and when did that start?

Futuristic|Rational.recognize: You think your way toward what is coming rather than merely hoping, so your picture holds together under questioning. But careful thinking applied to the future produces something that sounds like knowledge, and you defend a projection with the confidence appropriate to a fact.
Futuristic|Rational.ask: What is the actual likelihood of this, and would you bet on it?

Futuristic|Rational and Practical.recognize: You solve today's problem in a way that also serves where things are heading, so your fixes do not have to be undone later. But you will not accept a solution that only works now, and sometimes the only thing available is the one that only works now.
Futuristic|Rational and Practical.ask: What are you refusing to do because it is not the permanent answer?
