Futuristic|Receptive.recognize: You take in what people bring you and fit it into where you see things going, so contributions land somewhere rather than disappearing. But everything gets absorbed into your picture, and someone who offered a correction finds it has been converted into support.
Futuristic|Receptive.ask: Who disagreed with you and left the room thinking they had agreed?

Futuristic|Reliable.recognize: You honour what you promised, and you promised it against something you could clearly see, which is why your commitments are ambitious rather than safe. But the picture moves and the promise does not, and you end up delivering things you no longer think are worth delivering.
Futuristic|Reliable.ask: Which of your commitments would you cancel if nobody would notice?

Futuristic|Research-Oriented.recognize: You check whether the thing you can see is actually supported, which puts you well ahead of people who only speculate. But the future does not produce proof on demand, and you can spend a long time looking for confirmation of something that by definition has not happened.
Futuristic|Research-Oriented.ask: What would count as proof here, and can it exist yet?

Futuristic|Results Oriented.recognize: You complete things and you complete them toward something larger, so your completed work compounds instead of sitting alone. But the larger thing justifies almost any cost in your accounting, and the people paying that cost did not agree to the larger thing.
Futuristic|Results Oriented.ask: Who is paying for a goal they never signed up for?

Futuristic|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You care for people while holding what they could grow into, and that combination makes your care feel like belief rather than pity. But you reach for the encouraging future when someone is in pain, and being told about later is sometimes the least warm thing available.
Futuristic|Sensitive and Warm.ask: What would it cost you to say nothing about later?

Futuristic|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You tune how you present a big ambition so it does not frighten people, and that is why yours gets a hearing when other people's does not. But you keep trimming it to fit the room, and the version you have been describing for a year is smaller than the one you actually hold.
Futuristic|Sensitive to Others.ask: What is the real size of this, and who has heard it?

Futuristic|Sociable.recognize: You enjoy people and you talk about where things are going, so you end up connected to everyone who is interested in what is next. But those conversations are about a destination rather than a life, and you have many people who know your plans and few who know you.
Futuristic|Sociable.ask: Who could tell someone what kind of week you have had?

Futuristic|Spontaneous.recognize: You take an opening the moment it appears because you already know what it could turn into, and that is how you catch things other people study until they are gone. But you also redirect on those openings, and the thing you left is somebody else's job now.
Futuristic|Spontaneous.ask: What did you drop when you moved, and who picked it up?

Futuristic|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You take on what is in front of you and keep it pointed at something larger, so the daily work adds up instead of just repeating. But you also do it yourself because explaining the larger point takes longer than doing the task, and nothing gets handed over.
Futuristic|Strong Practical Skills.ask: What would you have to explain in order to give this away?

Futuristic|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take on responsibility for things that will not come due for years, which is why long promises get honoured around you when they usually do not. But you accept them against a future in which you have more capacity, and that future has not arrived once.
Futuristic|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: What did you agree to on the assumption that things would have eased by now?

Futuristic|Strong-willed.recognize: You will not be talked out of a direction, and for something that takes years that stubbornness is often the only thing that keeps it alive. But conviction about the future has no evidence to correct it, and yours can only be tested by time you have already spent.
Futuristic|Strong-willed.ask: What is the latest point at which you would still be willing to be wrong about this?

Futuristic|Supportive.recognize: You support people toward what they are capable of rather than what they are currently doing, and for the right person at the right moment that is transformative. But you support the trajectory, and if someone stops moving your support quietly withdraws before you have said anything.
Futuristic|Supportive.ask: Who used to have your attention and no longer does, and did you ever tell them why?

Futuristic|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with people through long stretches because you can see who they are becoming, and that is a rarer kind of loyalty than staying out of habit. But it is loyalty to a version of them, and if they choose a different life you will feel it as something they did to you.
Futuristic|Very Loyal.ask: Who would you still be close to if they gave up on the thing you admire them for?

Futuristic|Very Responsible.recognize: You take the blame for outcomes that will not be visible for years, which is a form of responsibility most people avoid because nobody is checking. But you also hold yourself liable for consequences you only predicted, and you carry blame for things that have not yet gone wrong.
Futuristic|Very Responsible.ask: What are you already holding yourself responsible for that has not happened?

Ideation|Altruistic.recognize: You hand people your best thinking without asking for anything, and a fair amount of what other teams are running started in your mouth. You do not mind that. What you have never checked is whether any of it landed, so you keep giving away more and better.
Ideation|Altruistic.ask: Which of the things you gave away actually got used?

Ideation|Analytical.recognize: You come up with something and immediately take it apart, so what survives is worth hearing. But the two happen so fast and so privately that people only meet the finished thought, and they assume you are certain when you are still mid-argument with yourself.
Ideation|Analytical.ask: What are you still arguing with yourself about that you presented as settled?

Ideation|Bold.recognize: You will say the untested thing in front of people who can act on it, which is how genuinely new work gets started. The cost is that some of it was never meant to leave your head, and you find out which ones only after somebody has begun building.
Ideation|Bold.ask: What did you throw out casually that somebody took as a decision?

Ideation|Calm and Practical.recognize: You produce unusual thinking in an unremarkable tone, so it gets heard on its merits instead of being dismissed as excitable. But the same flatness means nobody can tell which of your suggestions you actually care about, and the one that mattered gets filed alongside the rest.
Ideation|Calm and Practical.ask: Of everything you said in that meeting, which one did you want them to take?

Ideation|Charismatic.recognize: You put something new into a room and people want in before they understand it, which is how you gather momentum in minutes. That is also the risk. The pull is coming from you rather than from the thing, and it will not survive the first week you are absent.
Ideation|Charismatic.ask: Would this still be moving if you stopped talking about it?

Ideation|Charming.recognize: You make an odd suggestion land lightly, so people consider things they would have rejected from anyone else. That is a real skill. But lightness is also how you protect yourself, and if the idea is dismissed you have already made it small enough not to have cost you.
Ideation|Charming.ask: What have you offered as a joke that you actually meant?

Ideation|Clear Communication.recognize: You take something strange and say it so simply that people forget how strange it was, which is why your thinking travels. But the simple version is the one that spreads, and it arrives without the part that made it worth doing.
Ideation|Clear Communication.ask: What is the version of this that only you are still holding?

Ideation|Creative.recognize: You have one instinct doubled here with nothing holding the other end. Everything you touch turns into a new possibility, including the things that were finished, and you cannot tell the difference between improving something and starting it again. The room around you is full of near-versions.
Ideation|Creative.ask: What did you already get right and then reopen?

Ideation|Curious.recognize: You reach three answers nobody has tried before you have finished asking the question. That combination is where original work comes from. But an answer that interests you is not the same as one that helps, and you rarely check which kind you produced.
Ideation|Curious.ask: Was that useful, or just interesting?

Ideation|Decisive Action.recognize: You think of it and you back it in the same breath, so things get started around you that would otherwise die in discussion. But you back the newest thought rather than the best one, and the newest is simply whatever arrived most recently.
Ideation|Decisive Action.ask: Is this better than what you were committed to last month, or just newer?

Ideation|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with a thing long after the excitement has gone, which is rare for someone whose mind moves like yours. But your loyalty attaches to the original thought rather than to what it has become, and you are still defending a version that stopped existing a year ago.
Ideation|Dedicated.ask: Is what you are protecting still the thing you first had?

Ideation|Determined.recognize: You keep going on something unproven long past the point where a reasonable person would stop, and occasionally that is exactly why it works. But you cannot easily tell perseverance from attachment, and neither can anyone watching you.
Ideation|Determined.ask: What would you need to see to let this one go?

Ideation|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You notice the small anomaly and immediately imagine what it could mean, so you find opportunities inside things other people log as errors. But you also build a theory on one observation, and you present the theory rather than the observation.
Ideation|Diligent and Observant.ask: How many times have you actually seen this happen?

Ideation|Direct.recognize: You say the new thing plainly, without cushioning it, so nobody has to guess what you meant. That saves everyone time. But an unfamiliar suggestion delivered flatly sounds like a criticism of whatever exists now, and people defend rather than consider.
Ideation|Direct.ask: Who heard your last suggestion as an attack on their work?

Ideation|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You share what you are actually thinking while it is still forming, which lets people into a process most keep hidden. It is generous and it is disorienting. Half of what you say is provisional and you do not mark which half.
Ideation|Direct and Authentic.ask: How would someone know when you have made up your mind?

Ideation|Direct and Honest.recognize: You offer the alternative nobody asked for, before the decision is locked, which has saved work more than once. But it arrives as a better option rather than as a question, and the person who spent a month on the current plan hears it as a verdict on them.
Ideation|Direct and Honest.ask: How would you say that so it does not sound like their work was wasted?

Ideation|Disciplined.recognize: You hold a structure that lets you stay productive despite a mind that would otherwise go everywhere, and that is why you finish more than people like you usually do. But the structure was built to contain you, and you now treat it as a standard for everyone.
Ideation|Disciplined.ask: Which of your rules exist because of you rather than because of the work?

Ideation|Easygoing.recognize: You are not anxious when new thinking arrives, so you can hold a half-formed thought for months without forcing it. Some of your best work needed exactly that. But nothing external ever calls it in, and some of those thoughts have been held for years.
Ideation|Easygoing.ask: What have you been sitting on long enough that it is now overdue?

Ideation|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You find a completely different way to do the thing, not just a faster version of the current way, which is where the big savings actually come from. But you redesign faster than anyone can adopt, and people are still learning your last answer.
Ideation|Efficient Organizer.ask: How long has your team had to live with your last change?

Ideation|Empathetic.recognize: You feel what somebody is carrying and immediately start imagining a way out for them, which is why your help is original rather than generic. But you offer the way out before they have finished describing the weight, and being solved is not being heard.
Ideation|Empathetic.ask: Who wanted to finish the sentence before you answered it?

Ideation|Energetic.recognize: Your output is high and it is all new, which makes you enormously valuable and quite tiring to work near. Everyone else is executing your last three thoughts while you are producing the next three, and the gap between you and them widens by the week.
Ideation|Energetic.ask: How far behind you is the person doing the actual work?

Ideation|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You keep your thinking sorted, which is why your unusual thoughts can be found again instead of being lost. That is genuinely rare in someone with your mind. But sorting is also comfortable, and you will spend an afternoon filing thoughts rather than testing one.
Ideation|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: When did you last take one of them out and try it?

Ideation|Enthusiastic.recognize: You produce new thinking and open excitement at once, so people catch it from you before they have evaluated it. That is how things get moving. It is also why your enthusiasm has stopped being information, because you have been this excited about six things this quarter.
Ideation|Enthusiastic.ask: How many of the things you were excited about this year still exist?

Ideation|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You are running the same instinct twice with nothing here to slow it. Options arrive faster than any room can hold, and the quantity itself becomes the obstacle. Nobody can choose from what you produce, so they wait for you to choose, and you never do.
Ideation|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: What would happen if you brought exactly one option to the next meeting?

Ideation|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You can make an unfamiliar thought vivid enough that a room adopts it in ten minutes, which is a real form of leadership. But you are far better at describing it than at doing it, and the room keeps mistaking the description for progress.
Ideation|Excellent Communicators.ask: How much of this exists outside the telling?

Ideation|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You design the new thing and the machinery to run it at the same time, which is why yours actually get built where other people's stay talk. But you design the machinery for the version you have today, and you will have a different version by Friday.
Ideation|Excellent Organizers.ask: What did your team build that you had already moved past?

Ideation|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You read the room and shape the thought to fit who is in it, so your suggestions land where a blunter person's would not. But you shape it enough that different people have heard different versions, and none of them is quite the one you believe.
Ideation|Excellent People Skills.ask: Has anyone heard the version you would defend?

Ideation|Future Focused.recognize: You imagine what could exist and then work out when it becomes possible, so your thinking has a date attached rather than floating free. But the date is always a few years out, and you have been living in that window for a long time without arriving.
Ideation|Future Focused.ask: What could you start this month that does not require the world to change first?

Ideation|Generous.recognize: You give your thinking away without keeping score, and a good deal of what other people are known for started with you. That does not bother you the way it bothers everyone watching. But it means your contribution is invisible when it matters, including to the people deciding your future.
Ideation|Generous.ask: Who knows what you actually contributed this year?

Ideation|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You can make the thing you imagined, which puts you far ahead of people who only have the thought. But the making yields another idea halfway through, and you have a workshop of things at seventy per cent that were each abandoned for something better.
Ideation|Good Practical Skills.ask: What is nearly done that you left to start something else?

Ideation|Good at Connecting with Others.recognize: You see what two people could make together before either has thought of it, and some of those pairings become real things. But you are matching an imagined project, and the two people are left to work out whether they actually want it.
Ideation|Good at Connecting with Others.ask: How many of those pairings did you follow up on?

Ideation|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You meet a stuck situation with a new angle and good humour, which is why people feel better after talking to you even when nothing was solved. But an angle is not always what is wanted, and some problems needed to be sat with rather than reframed.
Ideation|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: What have you turned into an interesting problem when it was just a hard one?

Ideation|Grounded.recognize: You produce a great deal of new thinking and you still know what you will not trade away, which keeps you from chasing everything. But the two sides argue constantly and only you can hear it, so your decisions look arbitrary from outside.
Ideation|Grounded.ask: What is the thing you would not give up here, and have you said it out loud?

Ideation|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You try the new thought at once rather than discussing it, so you learn in an afternoon what a committee would take a quarter to guess at. But you try it on whatever is in front of you, and the thing in front of you is often somebody else's live work.
Ideation|Hands-on and Observant.ask: Whose live work did you use as your test bench?

Ideation|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You make something work out of parts that were never meant for it, and the result is genuinely clever. But clever and durable are different, and you lose interest at exactly the point where the thing would need to be made properly.
Ideation|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What is running on something clever that nobody else could repair?

Ideation|Hardworking.recognize: You put real hours behind your thinking, which is why yours turns into something instead of remaining conversation. But you also work hard on the ones that should have been dropped, because the hours already spent make a weak thought feel worth saving.
Ideation|Hardworking.ask: What are you still labouring over only because you have already put so much in?

Ideation|Honest.recognize: You will say plainly when one of yours was wrong, which is rarer than it sounds for someone whose ideas are so closely identified with them. But you drop them without ceremony, and the people who invested in the last one find out casually.
Ideation|Honest.ask: Who reorganised around the one you have quietly abandoned?

Ideation|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state the alternative without dressing it up, and you state it early enough to matter. That is worth a great deal to a team. But you state it with the confidence of something proven, when what you have is one afternoon of thinking.
Ideation|Honest and Direct.ask: How much work is actually behind the thing you just asserted?

Ideation|Idealistic.recognize: You imagine how something should be and you are resourceful enough to sketch how, so your standards arrive with directions attached. But every real version arrives compromised, and you experience each one as a failure rather than as a thing that now exists.
Ideation|Idealistic.ask: What is working right now that you have never allowed yourself to count?

Ideation|Imaginative.recognize: You have one faculty wearing two names with nothing on the other side of it. You can generate whole worlds and populate them convincingly, and none of it requires anything from reality, which is precisely why so little of it has ever met reality.
Ideation|Imaginative.ask: What is the smallest piece of this that could exist by Friday?

Ideation|Independent.recognize: You develop your thinking alone, so it stays strange instead of being sanded down by consensus, and strange is where the value is. But nothing gets tested until it is finished, and by then you are attached enough that criticism arrives as rejection.
Ideation|Independent.ask: Who sees it while it is still rough?

Ideation|Informed.recognize: You know what is happening in your field and you recombine it into things nobody has tried, which is where most genuinely new work actually comes from. But you also mistake having read widely for having verified, and some of your foundations are other people's summaries.
Ideation|Informed.ask: What are you building on that you have never checked yourself?

Ideation|Insightful.recognize: You see through to what a problem really is and immediately produce three ways around it, often before anyone has finished stating it. That speed is why you are in the room. But nobody watched you get there, so your best contributions are received as assertions.
Ideation|Insightful.ask: When did you last show the middle of your thinking instead of the end?

Ideation|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You take somebody's rough thought and hand it back better, and they leave feeling capable rather than corrected. That is a rare thing to be able to do. But the improved version is yours, and over time people bring you fragments and expect you to finish them.
Ideation|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who has stopped developing their own thinking because you always complete it?

Ideation|Knowledgeable.recognize: You have a wide reservoir to draw on and you connect across it, which is why your suggestions come from places nobody expects. But breadth also makes it easy to dismiss a simple objection, and the person raising it is sometimes closer to the work than you are.
Ideation|Knowledgeable.ask: Who told you it would not work, and had they actually tried it?

Ideation|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You remain with people through the long uninteresting stretches, which is unusual for someone who is drawn to what is new. But your patience is for people and not for projects, and the ones you are closest to have learned not to expect the same from your attention to their work.
Ideation|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: Who has your loyalty but not your interest, and do they know?

Ideation|Observant.recognize: You notice things others walk past and you immediately ask what could be made of them, which is where your best material comes from. But noticing feeds you faster than you can act, and the backlog of interesting things you have seen keeps growing.
Ideation|Observant.ask: What have you noticed repeatedly and never done anything about?

Ideation|Open-Minded.recognize: You will take any suggestion seriously and build on it, so people bring you things they would not risk elsewhere. That receptiveness is why your circle produces more than it should. But you build on all of them equally, and nobody can tell what you would defend.
Ideation|Open-Minded.ask: Which of these would you fight for?

Ideation|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have a way of capturing what arrives so it does not evaporate, which is why more of your thinking survives than most people's. But capture is not commitment, and your system is now a large well-maintained record of things you have not done.
Ideation|Organized and Effective.ask: How many of the things in your system are older than a year?

Ideation|Original.recognize: You have two names for the same drive and no brake on it here. You cannot leave a working approach alone, and difference has become its own justification, so you sometimes replace something that was fine with something that is merely unfamiliar.
Ideation|Original.ask: What working thing did you replace with something merely different?

Ideation|Passionate.recognize: Your ideas take all of you when they take hold, and that intensity is why some of them actually get built. But intensity does not last as long as projects do, and everyone around you has learned to wait and see whether this one holds.
Ideation|Passionate.ask: Who is waiting to find out whether you mean it this time?

Ideation|Perceptive.recognize: You sense what is unsaid in a room and turn it into something addressable, which lets groups discuss what they were avoiding. But you also construct an explanation for what you sensed, and you present the explanation with the same confidence as the sensing.
Ideation|Perceptive.ask: What did you decide someone was feeling without ever asking?

Ideation|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You produce a way around a wall and lift the mood at once, which keeps things alive that would otherwise stall. But you reach for the new angle whenever things get heavy, and some walls needed to be acknowledged rather than routed around.
Ideation|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: What problem keeps coming back because you keep finding a way past it?

Ideation|Principled.recognize: Your convictions are your own rather than inherited, worked out from first principles, and that makes them coherent in a way most people's are not. But you also rebuild them periodically, and the people who organised around your last position were not told.
Ideation|Principled.ask: Who is still operating on a position you have since left behind?

Ideation|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You begin the new thing yourself rather than waiting for approval, which is why some of yours exist at all. But starting is your strongest suit and finishing is not, so you have begun several things that now need somebody else to rescue.
Ideation|Proactive Initiative.ask: What have you started that somebody else is now responsible for finishing?

Ideation|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You produce a fresh answer in the time most people take to understand the question, which is why you are useful when things are moving. But you answer at that pace even when nothing is urgent, and thinking that needed a week gets three minutes.
Ideation|Quick Thinkers.ask: What deserved more time than you gave it this month?

Ideation|Rational.recognize: You generate freely and then hold each one against whether it actually follows, so what you bring forward tends to survive scrutiny. But you only trust what can be argued, and some of your best material arrived as an instinct you then discarded for lack of a case.
Ideation|Rational.ask: What did you discard for lack of an argument?

Ideation|Rational and Practical.recognize: You come up with something genuinely new and then check that somebody could actually use it, which is why yours get taken up where cleverer ones do not. But application is your only filter, and you will discard something remarkable because you cannot yet name what it is for.
Ideation|Rational and Practical.ask: What did you drop because you could not see the application yet?

Ideation|Receptive.recognize: You take in what people offer and build something better from it, so contributions come back to their owners improved. That makes you a good person to think near. But you build on whatever arrives most recently, and your direction is set by whoever spoke last.
Ideation|Receptive.ask: Whose thinking are you currently following, and did you choose it?

Ideation|Reliable.recognize: You honour what you said even when the thing you said stopped interesting you, which is unusual and expensive for a mind like yours. But nobody sees the cost, so they go on asking, and you go on agreeing while the work you actually want to do waits.
Ideation|Reliable.ask: Which of your promises is blocking the work you actually want?

Ideation|Research-Oriented.recognize: You come up with something and then go and find out whether it is true, which is the whole discipline in two steps and almost nobody does both. But the checking is slower than the generating, and the queue of unchecked thoughts behind the current one keeps growing.
Ideation|Research-Oriented.ask: How many of yours are waiting on you to confirm them?

Ideation|Results Oriented.recognize: You take one all the way to something delivered, which separates you from most people who think the way you do. But you deliver the one you started, and by the time it lands you know a better version, and you ship the old one anyway.
Ideation|Results Oriented.ask: What did you deliver that you had already outgrown?

Ideation|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You imagine what would help a particular person, not people in general, so what you offer fits them specifically. But you also make up reasons for their behaviour when you do not know, and you are kind to a version of them you constructed.
Ideation|Sensitive and Warm.ask: What story have you built about them in place of asking?

Ideation|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You test how something will land before you say it, so your stranger suggestions get a hearing instead of a reaction. But you trim as you go, and the thought that reaches the room has already lost the part that made it worth saying.
Ideation|Sensitive to Others.ask: What did you cut out of that before anyone heard it?

Ideation|Sociable.recognize: You think best out loud with other people, and conversation is genuinely where your material comes from rather than being a distraction from it. But you need an audience to think at all, and the thoughts that require solitude are the ones you never have.
Ideation|Sociable.ask: When did you last think something through with nobody there?

Ideation|Spontaneous.recognize: You act on the new thought the moment it arrives, which is how some of yours exist at all rather than dying in consideration. But you change course just as suddenly, and the people who joined the last direction find out when they notice you are gone.
Ideation|Spontaneous.ask: Who is still working on the thing you moved on from?

Ideation|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You can both think of it and make it, which means you rarely need anybody, and that is exactly the trap. Everything stays with you because handing it over would take longer than doing it, so nothing you have made can outlive your attention.

Ideation|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You feel responsible for the things you started, and that is why yours do not get abandoned the way people expect. But you started a great many, and duty keeps you attached to all of them at a level that no longer serves any of them.
Ideation|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: Which of these would you release if somebody gave you permission?

Ideation|Strong-willed.recognize: You will hold an unpopular position long enough for it to be proven, and sometimes it is. But holding is not your natural mode, so when you do plant yourself it is usually about the ones you were challenged on rather than the ones you were most sure of.
Ideation|Strong-willed.ask: Are you defending this because it is right, or because somebody attacked it?

Ideation|Supportive.recognize: You get behind other people's half-formed thinking and give it somewhere to go, which is why people bring you things early. But you improve as you support, and the person often ends up carrying something they no longer recognise as theirs.
Ideation|Supportive.ask: Whose project did you take over while trying to help?

Ideation|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with people you believe in and you keep finding new ways to be useful to them, which is a rare kind of steadiness from someone whose attention moves. But your loyalty is to a few, and everyone outside that circle gets a version of you that is easily distracted.
Ideation|Very Loyal.ask: Who is inside your circle, and who has worked out that they are not?

Ideation|Very Responsible.recognize: You own what happens to the things you set in motion, which is more than most people with your temperament do. But you set a great deal in motion, and you have taken on responsibility for outcomes that were never within your control.
Ideation|Very Responsible.ask: What are you carrying the blame for that was never actually yours to decide?

Input|Altruistic.recognize: You keep things because somebody might need them, and often somebody does, so what you have put aside has quietly rescued people more than once. But the keeping is for others and the cost is yours, and nobody has ever counted what carrying it takes.
Input|Altruistic.ask: What are you holding on to for people who have never asked for it?

Input|Analytical.recognize: You collect widely and then take apart what you collected, so you own your material rather than merely possessing it. But taking apart is slower than collecting, and most of what you have brought in has never been through that second step.
Input|Analytical.ask: What proportion of what you have saved have you actually been through?

Input|Bold.recognize: You will move on something risky because you have quietly built up what you would need if it went wrong, which makes your risks better funded than they appear. But the buffer keeps growing, and the point where it was enough passed some time ago.
Input|Bold.ask: What would have to be true for you to feel ready, and is it already true?

Input|Calm and Practical.recognize: You do not panic, partly because you usually have what is needed already put by, and in a crisis that steadiness is worth more than speed. But the same calm means you rarely raise the alarm, and you will absorb a shortage quietly until it becomes somebody else's emergency.
Input|Calm and Practical.ask: What shortage are you absorbing on everyone's behalf?

Input|Charismatic.recognize: You draw people in and you have something for each of them, which is why your relationships feel abundant rather than transactional. But you offer material more readily than you offer yourself, and a great many people have received something from you without ever getting close.
Input|Charismatic.ask: Who knows you rather than what you can supply?

Input|Charming.recognize: You put people at rest and they tell you things, and you keep what they tell you, which is why you know a great deal about a great many people. But nothing you hold ever gets discarded, and some of what you know about someone is years out of date.
Input|Charming.ask: What in your picture of somebody is out of date?

Input|Clear Communication.recognize: You can take a mountain of material and give somebody the one usable sentence, which is why people come to you rather than to the source. But the sentence is a selection, and you make the selection alone, and nobody sees what you set aside.
Input|Clear Communication.ask: What did you leave out, and would they have chosen differently?

Input|Creative.recognize: Your work draws on more material than most people have access to, so it has depth and unexpected connections. But collecting feels productive in the same way making does, and you can spend a season acquiring and mistake it for a season of work.
Input|Creative.ask: What did you actually make this year?

Input|Curious.recognize: You have the same appetite twice over, with nothing on the other side asking what it is for. Everything is interesting and everything gets kept, and the volume has stopped being an advantage. You are the best-supplied person in the room and the least able to say what you are supplied for.
Input|Curious.ask: What is all of this for?

Input|Decisive Action.recognize: You decide firmly and you decide from a deeper base of material than most people have, so your calls hold up. But the material also gives you a reason to wait, and you can always name one more thing worth having before you move.
Input|Decisive Action.ask: What would you have to accept in order to start with what you already have?

Input|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with things and you keep everything belonging to them, so nothing you commit to ever loses its history. But you also keep the weight of every past commitment, and you are carrying material from things that finished years ago.
Input|Dedicated.ask: What could you put down that ended a long time ago?

Input|Determined.recognize: You keep going and you keep supplying yourself for the next stretch, which is why you last where better-resourced people give up. But the supplying has become part of the effort, and preparing for the next stage now takes longer than the stage does.
Input|Determined.ask: How much of your effort goes into getting ready rather than doing?

Input|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You notice small things and you keep a record of them, so you can show a pattern where somebody else has only an impression. That is genuinely powerful. But you keep the record whether or not you intend to use it, and some of it has become a private case against people.
Input|Diligent and Observant.ask: What are you keeping track of that you have never raised with the person?

Input|Direct.recognize: You say it plainly and you can produce what backs it up on the spot, which makes you very hard to wave away. But producing it feels to the other person like being presented with a file, and they came for a conversation.
Input|Direct.ask: Did you need to show the evidence, or did you want to?

Input|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You tell people what you actually think and you have thought about it with more material than they expect, so your candour has substance behind it. But you also lay out the whole of your reasoning, and people who wanted your view get your working instead.
Input|Direct and Authentic.ask: What is your answer, without the background?

Input|Direct and Honest.recognize: You offer what you know before somebody has to ask, which stops people making decisions in the dark. But you offer everything you know, and burying the important item in the complete account is its own way of not saying it.
Input|Direct and Honest.ask: What was the one thing in there that actually mattered?

Input|Disciplined.recognize: You keep things properly, so they can be found and used, which is what separates a resource from a pile. But upkeep is now a standing commitment, and you have never asked whether it is worth the hours it takes.
Input|Disciplined.ask: How many hours a month does your collection cost you?

Input|Easygoing.recognize: You accumulate without anxiety and you are not precious about any of it, which makes you generous with what you have. But nothing ever forces a sort, and the useful things are now mixed in with everything else so thoroughly that you go and find them fresh instead.
Input|Easygoing.ask: When did you last find something you already had?

Input|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You keep a great deal and you keep it in a way that makes it fast to reach, which is why your abundance is a strength rather than a burden. But you optimise the holding rather than the using, and a well-organised store is still a store.
Input|Efficient Organizer.ask: What have you improved the storage of this month instead of using?

Input|Empathetic.recognize: You sense what somebody needs and you often already have it, so your help arrives fast and fits. But you also take in what they are feeling and keep that too, and you are holding the emotional residue of conversations everyone else has forgotten.
Input|Empathetic.ask: What are you still carrying from somebody who has already moved on?

Input|Energetic.recognize: You have the drive to keep bringing things in and the stamina to keep on top of them, which is why your collection has not collapsed the way most do. But you have never tested whether you could stop, and you might find that the gathering is what the energy is for.
Input|Energetic.ask: What would you do with the time if you stopped adding to it?

Input|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You put what you bring in where it belongs, so your abundance is navigable rather than chaotic. But the pleasure of putting things away is real and immediate where using them is neither, and you keep choosing the pleasure without noticing you chose.
Input|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: Which do you enjoy more, finding it or filing it?

Input|Enthusiastic.recognize: You get excited about what you have found and you pass it on, so people around you are better supplied than they would otherwise be. But you pass on the volume as well as the excitement, and somebody who asked a question receives a reading list.
Input|Enthusiastic.ask: How much of what you sent them do you think they got through?

Input|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You have more raw material than anyone in the room and you turn it into options quickly, which is why you are never short of possibilities. But possibilities are not decisions, and both of your instincts here produce more rather than fewer.
Input|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: What in your life is reducing the number of things, rather than increasing it?

Input|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You explain well and you have the depth behind it, so when you talk about something people can tell you know it rather than having read one article. But depth is also why you go long, and the room has often stopped listening before you have reached the useful part.
Input|Excellent Communicators.ask: Where in that explanation did people stop following?

Input|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You build systems that hold everything, and yours do not fall over the way most do, because you designed for the volume you actually have. But you designed for your volume, and everyone else has to operate a system built for a collection they do not have.
Input|Excellent Organizers.ask: Does anyone else use the system you built, or only you?

Input|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You remember what matters to people and you have something for them when it counts, which is why your relationships feel attentive rather than performed. But you are always slightly collecting during a conversation, and there are people you have never simply talked to.
Input|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who do you talk to without taking anything away from it?

Input|Future Focused.recognize: You put things aside for a version of the future you can actually see coming, which is why your preparation is aimed rather than anxious. But you prepare for several futures at once, and you are carrying provisions for at least two lives you will not live.
Input|Future Focused.ask: Which of the futures you are ready for are you not actually going to have?

Input|Generous.recognize: You give from what you have put by and you give without hesitation, so people around you are supplied from a source they cannot see. But you replace what you gave immediately, and the giving never actually reduces anything, which means it has never cost you what generosity usually costs.
Input|Generous.ask: What have you given away that you actually missed?

Input|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You have both the materials and the skill, so you make things instead of waiting for the right conditions. But you also acquire the materials for projects you have only considered, and the shelf of things bought for something you never started keeps getting longer.
Input|Good Practical Skills.ask: What did you buy for a project that never began?

Input|Good at Connecting with Others.recognize: You know who knows what, and you connect people from a mental index nobody else has, which makes you unusually valuable in any network. But you keep every contact indefinitely, and maintaining a list that large is now most of what you do with people.
Input|Good at Connecting with Others.ask: How many of the people you keep up with have you spoken to properly this year?

Input|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You lift people and you usually have something concrete to offer alongside the encouragement, which is why yours does not feel empty. But you reach for the useful thing to hand over when somebody is upset, and being handed a resource is not being comforted.
Input|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: Who wanted your attention and got a recommendation?

Input|Grounded.recognize: You are steady because you know what you have and what you stand on, and that security is not borrowed from anyone. But security built on possessions has a floor that keeps rising, and you would not now feel steady on what once felt like plenty.
Input|Grounded.ask: What amount would be enough, and has that number moved?

Input|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You would rather have the thing in front of you than read about it, so what you accumulate is real and tested rather than theoretical. But you acquire faster than you can work through, and much of what you have taken in has never actually been handled.
Input|Hands-on and Observant.ask: What have you had for over a year and never opened?

Input|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You can solve almost anything because you have the parts and the wit to combine them, and people bring you problems that have defeated better-equipped teams. But this is why nothing ever gets replaced properly, and your capability has become an argument against fixing anything at the root.
Input|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What has never been dealt with properly because you keep making it work?

Input|Hardworking.recognize: You put in real hours and you have built up something substantial as a result, which is why your position is more secure than it looks. But acquiring is work you enjoy, and the hours spent on it count in your own accounting as productive when much of it is not.
Input|Hardworking.ask: How much of last week's work would somebody else have called work?

Input|Honest.recognize: You own what you do not know, which is unusual for somebody who knows as much as you do, and it makes people trust the rest. But you follow that by going away and fixing the gap, and the person who asked never gets an answer to what they actually needed.
Input|Honest.ask: Who is still waiting while you go and find out properly?

Input|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state things directly and you can produce chapter and verse if challenged, so people rarely challenge you twice. But that is not always because you were right, and some of the silence around you is people deciding it is not worth the material you would bring.
Input|Honest and Direct.ask: Who has stopped disagreeing with you, and was it because you convinced them?

Input|Idealistic.recognize: You accumulate toward something better than what exists, so your collecting has a direction rather than being mere appetite. But the standard you are gathering toward keeps rising with what you learn, and you have never once felt ready to begin.
Input|Idealistic.ask: What would you need in order to start, and did you say the same thing last year?

Input|Imaginative.recognize: You take in a great deal and it becomes raw material for things nobody has made, which is a genuinely different use of a collection than most people manage. But you can also live in what you have gathered, and browsing has become a place you go rather than a thing you do.
Input|Imaginative.ask: Where does your attention go when you are avoiding something?

Input|Independent.recognize: You have what you need and you do not have to ask anyone, which is real freedom and you built it deliberately. But self-sufficiency is also how you stopped needing people, and needing people is most of how relationships stay alive.
Input|Independent.ask: When did you last ask somebody for something you could have got yourself?

Input|Informed.recognize: You have one appetite doubled here and it has no exit. You know what is happening and you keep the record of it, and both halves reward taking in more, so nothing in your habits ever says that is enough. Being current has become a permanent job.
Input|Informed.ask: What would you lose if you stopped following it for a month?

Input|Insightful.recognize: You see through to what matters and you have the material to support it, which makes your judgment unusually well founded. But you reach the insight early and then keep gathering anyway, and the extra material is reassurance rather than evidence.
Input|Insightful.ask: At what point did you know, and how much have you done since?

Input|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You remember what people have done well and you can name specifics, which makes your encouragement land as recognition. But you keep the record of their difficulties too, and you protect people from things they have long since become able to handle.
Input|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who are you still shielding based on who they were?

Input|Knowledgeable.recognize: You have the same drive wearing two labels, and doubled it has no counterweight. What you hold is genuinely deep and genuinely useful. What has no brake is the acquiring, and there is nothing in you that ever declares a subject sufficiently covered.
Input|Knowledgeable.ask: What subject would you allow yourself to be finished with?

Input|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You remain with people and you hold everything that belongs to those relationships, so nothing gets lost between you. But you also keep the difficult parts, and a friendship that would have healed carries a record that you can still consult exactly.
Input|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: What do you remember about them that would be better forgotten?

Input|Observant.recognize: You take in what is happening and you retain it, so you can see slow changes that nobody without your recall would catch. But retention without a use is just weight, and you have seen several situations deteriorate while continuing to record them.
Input|Observant.ask: What are you keeping a record of instead of acting on?

Input|Open-Minded.recognize: You will take in a view you disagree with and keep it rather than discarding it, which is why your thinking has real range. But everything gets kept and nothing gets rejected, and a mind that never throws anything out cannot easily say what it holds.
Input|Open-Minded.ask: What have you actually concluded, after all of that?

Input|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have a system and it works, so what you take in is retrievable years later and that is a real advantage. But the system was designed for accumulation, not for use, and there is no step in it where something leaves.
Input|Organized and Effective.ask: What is your process for getting rid of things?

Input|Original.recognize: You gather what other people ignore, so your material is different from everyone else's and that is where your originality actually comes from. But you also collect the unusual because it is unusual, and a fair amount of what you hold is remarkable and useless.
Input|Original.ask: What have you kept only because nobody else has one?

Input|Passionate.recognize: You go all the way in when something takes hold of you and come back with everything there is on it, which is why your knowledge on a few subjects is exceptional. But the subject changes, and the material from the last one stays, complete and untouched.
Input|Passionate.ask: What did you go deep on and then never open again?

Input|Perceptive.recognize: You pick up on things and you store what you pick up, so what you conclude about a person is built from years rather than a moment. But you have also held impressions you never tested, and some of what you believe about somebody rests on one thing you noticed once.
Input|Perceptive.ask: What impression of them have you never put to the test?

Input|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You keep morale up and you have practical things to hand out alongside the encouragement, which makes you useful in a hard stretch rather than merely pleasant. But offering the useful thing is also how you leave, and you have handed people a resource on your way out of difficult conversations.
Input|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: When did you last stay in a conversation with nothing to offer?

Input|Principled.recognize: Your convictions are supported by more than feeling, and you can produce the grounds when it matters, which is why yours survive challenge. But you have also kept a record of who has fallen short, and you can produce that as readily.
Input|Principled.ask: What are you still holding against somebody, and have you told them?

Input|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You are already supplied when the need appears, so you can start while everybody else is still assembling, and that head start is genuinely yours. But the preparing feels like progress, and you can spend a year ready to begin without beginning.
Input|Proactive Initiative.ask: What are you fully prepared for and still have not started?

Input|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You answer quickly because you already have the material rather than because you are guessing, which makes that reliable where other people's is not. But you answer at that pace regardless, and a question that deserved fresh thinking gets something you had on the shelf.
Input|Quick Thinkers.ask: When did you last give an answer you had not given before?

Input|Rational.recognize: You argue from material rather than from impression, so your positions are hard to shift by rhetoric alone. But you also dismiss what cannot be supported by something you can produce, and some true things arrive with nothing attached.
Input|Rational.ask: What do you suspect is true but cannot show?

Input|Rational and Practical.recognize: You keep what has a use and you can usually name the use, which is why your collecting is defensible where other people's is hoarding. But the use is often hypothetical, and naming a possible purpose has become the way you justify keeping anything at all.
Input|Rational and Practical.ask: Which of these have you actually used, rather than could use?

Input|Receptive.recognize: You take in whatever people bring you, and they bring you a lot, because you are the one who does not turn things away. But you accept without filtering, and a good deal of what you hold was somebody else's decision to give you rather than yours to take.
Input|Receptive.ask: What are you keeping because somebody handed it to you?

Input|Reliable.recognize: You have it when it is needed and you always have, which is why people stopped holding their own and started asking you. But that arrangement was never agreed, and the cost of being everybody's supply has never appeared on anyone's list but yours.
Input|Reliable.ask: What are you providing that nobody has ever thanked you for?

Input|Research-Oriented.recognize: You have the same appetite twice, and both halves say get more before you decide. What you produce is well founded and it is late, and the lateness is not caution, it is that neither instinct here has ever been the one that says stop.
Input|Research-Oriented.ask: What is the deadline, and what would you have to accept in order to meet it?

Input|Results Oriented.recognize: You bring things to completion and you have the material to get through the difficult middle without stalling, which is why your projects do not die of missing pieces. But you also acquire during the middle, and some of what you called groundwork was avoidance with a receipt.
Input|Results Oriented.ask: What did you go and get instead of doing the hard part?

Input|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You know what a person likes and you have it ready, so your care shows up as something in the hand rather than words. That lands with people who distrust words. But it is also a way of caring at one remove, and some people needed the words.
Input|Sensitive and Warm.ask: Who have you given something to instead of telling them?

Input|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You take note of what unsettles each person and you work around it, so people find you unusually easy to be near. But you have built a large private register of everyone's sore points, and there are now conversations you will not start with anybody.
Input|Sensitive to Others.ask: What subject have you retired entirely because of one person's reaction?

Input|Sociable.recognize: You enjoy people and you keep every connection, so your circle is wide and long-standing in a way most people's are not. But keeping is not the same as tending, and the width is now maintained at the cost of any of it being deep.
Input|Sociable.ask: Who would you call at two in the morning?

Input|Spontaneous.recognize: You take the opportunity when it appears and you have the means to act on it, which is why your sudden moves succeed more often than they should. But you also acquire on a whim, and a fair proportion of what you own arrived because it was available rather than wanted.
Input|Spontaneous.ask: What did you take on simply because it was there?

Input|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You have the materials and the ability, so problems that stop other people are an afternoon for you. But that makes you the default for everything, and the accumulation is not only of things now, it is of other people's unfinished business.
Input|Strong Practical Skills.ask: How much of what you are carrying originally belonged to somebody else?

Input|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take on what you owe and you make sure you have what is needed to meet it, which is why you rarely fail anybody. But you accept duties on the strength of what you have put by, and your supplies are the reason you have said yes to more than you can hold.
Input|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: What did you agree to because you were the only one equipped for it?

Input|Strong-willed.recognize: You hold your position and you have the material behind it, so pressure alone will not shift you and should not. But you are hardest to move on the subjects where you have gathered most, and depth of preparation is not the same as being right.
Input|Strong-willed.ask: Where have you invested so much research that changing your mind has become expensive?

Input|Supportive.recognize: You supply somebody you have got behind with everything they could need, which is why the people you support tend to succeed. But you supply so completely that they never learn to find things themselves, and your support has become a dependency neither of you named.
Input|Supportive.ask: Who has stopped looking for things because you always have them?

Input|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with your people and you hold everything about them, which is why being known by you is a rare kind of being known. But that includes what they did wrong, and you can bring it out intact years later without meaning to wound.
Input|Very Loyal.ask: What have you brought up that they had hoped was gone?

Input|Very Responsible.recognize: You take the blame when it is yours and you can reconstruct exactly what happened because you kept everything, so your reckoning is unusually honest. But you kept everything, and you have a complete and permanent record of every occasion you fell short.
Input|Very Responsible.ask: What would you let yourself delete?

Intellection|Altruistic.recognize: You think carefully about how to help before you help, so what you give tends to fit rather than merely relieve your own discomfort. But the thinking takes time the person may not have, and there are people you never got to because you were still working out the right way.
Intellection|Altruistic.ask: Who got nothing from you while you worked out the right thing?

Intellection|Analytical.recognize: You have two names for one habit here, and together they have no floor. You will take a thing apart, sit with the pieces, and then take the pieces apart, and there is nothing in the process that ever declares itself complete. Most of your work happens where nobody can see it.
Intellection|Analytical.ask: What have you finished thinking about that you have never told anyone?

Intellection|Bold.recognize: You take a real risk when you finally go, and one you have thought all the way through, so your boldness is earned rather than reckless. But the thinking is invisible, and to everyone else you are somebody who does nothing for months and then does something startling.
Intellection|Bold.ask: Who was blindsided by a decision you had been making for a year?

Intellection|Calm and Practical.recognize: You are the steady one and the steadiness is real, because you have already thought through most of what could happen. But your calm reads as this being fine, and people take reassurance from a face that is actually just concentrating.
Intellection|Calm and Practical.ask: What are you worried about that nobody can tell you are worried about?

Intellection|Charismatic.recognize: You draw people in and what they find underneath has substance, which is why the pull lasts past the first conversation. But you need long stretches alone to be that person, and the pull you exert keeps producing demands on exactly the time that makes you worth knowing.
Intellection|Charismatic.ask: How much time alone did you actually get this month?

Intellection|Charming.recognize: You are easy company and there is a great deal going on behind it, so people enjoy you without ever feeling they have got to the bottom of you. That is by design. But the charm has become a way of leaving the room while still standing in it.
Intellection|Charming.ask: Who have you kept at a comfortable distance for years?

Intellection|Clear Communication.recognize: You have thought about it for a long time and you can say it in a sentence, which is why people trust your summaries. But the sentence took months and sounds like it took a moment, and you get treated as somebody with quick opinions rather than considered ones.
Intellection|Clear Communication.ask: Does anybody know how long you spent on that?

Intellection|Creative.recognize: You turn your work over so many times that it arrives coherent and deep, which is why it holds up. But turning it over is more pleasant than releasing it, and there is finished work of yours that nobody has seen because you are still considering it.

Intellection|Curious.recognize: You follow a question inward rather than outward, which is why your understanding goes deeper than the people asking the same questions. But inward has no boundary, and you have spent whole weeks on things you were never going to act on.
Intellection|Curious.ask: What did you think about all week that changed nothing?

Intellection|Decisive Action.recognize: You take a long time and then you move all at once and do not look back, which is a genuinely effective way to operate. But the long part is invisible and the fast part is not, so people learn to fear your decisions rather than trust your process.
Intellection|Decisive Action.ask: How could people watch you decide, rather than only see the result?

Intellection|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with hard things because thinking about them is not a cost to you, so you outlast people who need visible progress. But you can also stay with something in your head for years while doing nothing about it, and to you that still counts as commitment.
Intellection|Dedicated.ask: What have you been committed to without acting on for longer than a year?

Intellection|Determined.recognize: You do not let go of a problem, and the sustained attention is why you eventually solve things that defeat quicker people. But you also do not let go of problems that have no solution, and the same persistence keeps you circling something that was settled long ago.
Intellection|Determined.ask: What are you still working on that already has an answer you do not like?

Intellection|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You notice something small and then think about it until you understand why it happened, which is how you find causes rather than symptoms. But you do that with everything, and a stray remark somebody made in passing can occupy you for three days.
Intellection|Diligent and Observant.ask: What has been living rent-free in your head this week?

Intellection|Direct.recognize: You say what you concluded without softening it, and you concluded it carefully, so it is usually worth hearing. But it arrives fully formed after a long silence, and people experience it as a judgment handed down rather than a view offered.
Intellection|Direct.ask: When did you last say something before you had finished deciding?

Intellection|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You say things about yourself that are true and considered rather than performed, which is why people find you credible in a way that polished people are not. But you offer conclusions about yourself, not the process, and the version people meet is already resolved.
Intellection|Direct and Authentic.ask: What are you currently unresolved about that nobody knows?

Intellection|Direct and Honest.recognize: You offer the difficult observation without being asked, and because you have sat with it, it is precise. But precision about a person is not always a kindness, and the accuracy is what makes it hard to recover from.
Intellection|Direct and Honest.ask: What did you get exactly right that you wish you had said less exactly?

Intellection|Disciplined.recognize: You keep a structure around your days, which is the only reason a mind like yours produces anything at all rather than dissolving into thought. But the structure protects your thinking time above everything else, and the people in your life have learned they come after it.
Intellection|Disciplined.ask: What have you protected your thinking time from that deserved to interrupt it?

Intellection|Easygoing.recognize: You are unhurried and genuinely comfortable in your own head, so you can sit with an unresolved thing for a long time without strain. That patience is a real asset. But nothing internal ever presses, and some questions have been open for years because being open costs you nothing.
Intellection|Easygoing.ask: What have you left unresolved simply because it does not bother you?

Intellection|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You think about why the process exists before you change it, so what you cut is genuinely waste rather than something you did not understand. But the thinking takes longer than the cutting, and simple improvements wait months for your consideration.
Intellection|Efficient Organizer.ask: What obvious fix is waiting on you to think it through properly?

Intellection|Empathetic.recognize: You feel what somebody is going through and then you think about it afterwards, at length, which is why your understanding of people is unusually deep. But you keep processing after they have moved on, and you are still working through a conversation they have forgotten.
Intellection|Empathetic.ask: Whose difficulty are you still carrying that they have already put down?

Intellection|Energetic.recognize: You have real drive and it goes inward as much as outward, so you can sustain mental effort at a level that would flatten most people. But it does not switch off, and the thing that looks like stamina to everyone else feels from the inside like something you cannot stop.
Intellection|Energetic.ask: When did you last have an evening where your mind was quiet?

Intellection|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You sort your thinking as you go, which is why you can retrieve a conclusion from three years ago intact. But sorting thoughts is more satisfying than acting on them, and you have an immaculate internal architecture with very little built on the outside.
Intellection|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: What have you thought through completely and never begun?

Intellection|Enthusiastic.recognize: You want to share what you have worked out, and the depth behind your excitement makes it land differently from ordinary enthusiasm. But you share the conclusion of a long private process, and the person receiving it is being asked to catch up in one conversation.
Intellection|Enthusiastic.ask: How much of your thinking did they have to take on faith?

Intellection|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You produce a lot and you have already weighed most of it, which is why your contributions in a session are better sorted than everyone else's. But you weighed it alone, and the room never gets to see the ones you rejected, some of which were theirs to judge.
Intellection|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: What did you rule out on the group's behalf?

Intellection|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You speak well about things you have thought about deeply, so what you say has weight rather than fluency alone. But you are also using the conversation to finish your thinking, and the other person has become the surface you are working against.
Intellection|Excellent Communicators.ask: Was that a conversation, or were you thinking out loud at somebody?

Intellection|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You think a plan all the way through before anyone else sees it, so what you present is coherent and holds together under questioning. But it arrives complete, and people cannot contribute to something finished, so they either accept it or reject it whole.
Intellection|Excellent Organizers.ask: When did you last bring a plan that still had gaps in it?

Intellection|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You are good with people and you think about them afterwards, so you notice things about them that a purely social person would miss. But the thinking is where the relationship actually happens for you, and there are people you know deeply who have no idea.
Intellection|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who have you thought about a great deal and never told?

Intellection|Future Focused.recognize: You think forward carefully rather than merely hoping, so your sense of where things are going is reasoned and usually sound. But you also run every possible version, including the bad ones, and you have lived through several futures that never happened.
Intellection|Future Focused.ask: How many of the disasters you have thought through actually occurred?

Intellection|Generous.recognize: You give people your considered attention, which is a scarcer thing than money and you hand it out freely. But considered attention takes hours, and you have committed more of them than exist, so the people at the back of your queue receive nothing at all.
Intellection|Generous.ask: Who has been waiting longest for the thought you promised them?

Intellection|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You understand the thing all the way down before you make it, so what you make rarely has to be redone. But you also need to understand it all the way down, and you will not begin something you could learn by doing.
Intellection|Good Practical Skills.ask: What have you not started because you do not understand it well enough yet?

Intellection|Good at Connecting with Oth.recognize: You think about who two people are before putting them together, so your matches are considered rather than automatic. But you think about it for a long time, and a fair number of connections you were sure about have never actually been made.
Intellection|Good at Connecting with Oth.ask: Who have you meant to introduce for over a year?

Intellection|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You are pleasant to be around and there is real thought behind your optimism, so it does not collapse the moment something goes wrong. But the pleasantness is partly a surface you maintain while you work, and people have no idea how much you are carrying.
Intellection|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: Who thinks you are fine right now?

Intellection|Grounded.recognize: You know what you stand upon and you arrived at it yourself rather than inheriting it, which is why it survives pressure. But you also revisit it constantly in private, and the certainty everybody sees is not what it feels like from inside.
Intellection|Grounded.ask: What do people think you are sure about that you are not?

Intellection|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You work with your hands and think while you do it, which is why the doing produces understanding rather than just output. But you need the physical task to think properly, and when there is nothing to do with your hands the thinking turns on itself.
Intellection|Hands-on and Observant.ask: What do you do when you need to think and there is nothing to work on?

Intellection|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You solve things by understanding them rather than by trial, so your fixes address the actual cause. But you also cannot leave a solved problem alone, and you keep returning to something that works because you are still unsatisfied with why it works.
Intellection|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What working thing are you still turning over?

Intellection|Hardworking.recognize: You put in long hours and a good portion of them are invisible, because thinking looks like nothing from outside. That is why you are often the most tired person in a room that thinks you did least. But you also count the invisible hours, and nobody else can.
Intellection|Hardworking.ask: Who thinks you have an easy job?

Intellection|Honest.recognize: You are honest about your own errors because you have already examined them thoroughly before anyone raised them. But you examined them thoroughly, and the admission comes with an analysis nobody asked for and a self-assessment harsher than the situation warranted.
Intellection|Honest.ask: Would you accept that explanation from somebody else who had done it?

Intellection|Honest and Direct.recognize: You state your position clearly and you have earned it, so people know exactly where you stand and can rely on it. But you only state it once you are certain, and the months before that read to everyone else as having no view.
Intellection|Honest and Direct.ask: What do you think about the thing everyone assumes you are neutral on?

Intellection|Idealistic.recognize: You have thought carefully about how things ought to be, so your standards are coherent rather than merely high. But you have also thought about them a great deal more than you have tested them, and the gap between the worked-out version and any real one only widens.
Intellection|Idealistic.ask: What have you built in your head that has never had to survive contact with anything?

Intellection|Imaginative.recognize: You can construct something elaborate internally and hold it there indefinitely, and the elaboration is genuinely good. But both of these live inside, and there is nothing in the pairing that ever requires anything to come out.
Intellection|Imaginative.ask: What is the first external step, and what would make you take it this week?

Intellection|Independent.recognize: You work things out for yourself and you do not need agreement, which means your conclusions are genuinely yours. But nothing you conclude ever meets resistance until it is final, and a mistake made early can survive for years unchallenged.
Intellection|Independent.ask: Who is qualified to tell you that you are wrong, and when did you last let them?

Intellection|Informed.recognize: You know what is going on and you think about what it means rather than merely relaying it, which is why your read is worth more than a summary. But you think about everything you take in, and the volume of news you follow has become a volume of thinking you cannot finish.
Intellection|Informed.ask: What would you stop following if you had to cut half of it?

Intellection|Insightful.recognize: You have the same faculty under two names, and doubled it goes deep rather than wide. You reach the bottom of things nobody else has reached, and you also keep going past the bottom, and there is nothing here that ever says you have arrived.
Intellection|Insightful.ask: What have you already understood that you are still working on?

Intellection|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: Your encouragement is specific because you have actually thought about the person, so it lands as being seen rather than being flattered. But you think before you speak, and there are people who needed something from you in the moment and got your silence.
Intellection|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who needed you to say something immediately, and what stopped you?

Intellection|Knowledgeable.recognize: You hold a great deal and you have thought about all of it, which is why your knowledge is usable rather than merely stored. But the thinking makes you certain, and certainty built alone is difficult for anyone else to dent.
Intellection|Knowledgeable.ask: Who was the last person to dent something you knew well?

Intellection|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.recognize: You remain with people and you think about them while you do, so your loyalty is considered rather than habitual. But you process difficulties internally rather than raising them, and things have been resolved inside your head that the other person never knew were problems.
Intellection|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.ask: What did you work through alone that they should have been part of?

Intellection|Observant.recognize: You see what is happening and you think about what it means before you respond, which is why you rarely misjudge a situation. But the thinking takes as long as it takes, and by the time you have understood something the moment to act on it has passed.
Intellection|Observant.ask: What did you work out only after it stopped mattering?

Intellection|Open-Minded.recognize: You will genuinely consider a view you dislike, and consider it properly rather than performing consideration, which is rarer than anyone admits. But you can hold several positions at once indefinitely, and holding them is comfortable enough that you never have to land.
Intellection|Open-Minded.ask: What have you been weighing for so long that the decision has made itself?

Intellection|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have a way of working that protects the long stretches your thinking needs, and that is why you produce depth where busier people produce volume. But that way of working assumes uninterrupted time, and you have become difficult to work with for anyone whose day does not look like yours.
Intellection|Organized and Effective.ask: What does working with you require from other people that you have never said out loud?

Intellection|Original.recognize: You arrive at unusual positions because you actually worked them out rather than adopting them, so your differences are substantive. But you worked them out alone, and you cannot always tell whether a position is unusual because it is better or because nobody checked it.
Intellection|Original.ask: Which of your views has ever been tested against somebody who knows the subject?

Intellection|Passionate.recognize: You think constantly about whatever you care about, and the combination produces a depth of engagement that most people never reach on anything. But it does not have an off position, and the thing you love is also the thing that is running in your head at three in the morning.
Intellection|Passionate.ask: What is the cost of caring about this as much as you do?

Intellection|Perceptive.recognize: You pick up on something and then think it through, so your conclusions about people are considered rather than snap judgments. But thinking about an impression does not test it, and a long-considered guess can feel like knowledge while remaining a guess.
