Significance|Enthusiastic.recognize: You get other people excited about something big, and your excitement is real, which is why it works even on the cynical ones. The gap is that you need the thing to stay big in order to stay excited, and projects that shrink honestly tend to lose you.
Significance|Enthusiastic.ask: What did you lose interest in once it got smaller?

Significance|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You produce plenty of ideas and you gravitate to the ones with scale attached, so you rarely spend time on the trivially achievable. The risk is that the modest idea you passed over was the one that would have worked, and nobody was going to be impressed by it.
Significance|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: Which small idea did you pass over?

Significance|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You can hold a room and make what you are describing feel important, which is why your projects attract support that comparable ones do not. The cost is that a talent for making things sound consequential works just as well on things that are not.
Significance|Excellent Communicators.ask: What have you made sound bigger than it actually is?

Significance|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You can assemble the machinery a large ambition actually requires, so your plans are not merely hopes. The gap is that scale becomes the test of whether something was worth doing, and a modest thing done well will never feel like enough to you.
Significance|Excellent Organizers.ask: Has a modest result ever felt like enough?

Significance|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You are good with people and you use it to get in front of the ones who matter, which is why your work finds an audience. The risk is that a relationship kept because of who somebody is has a shelf life, and both of you can feel when it expires.
Significance|Excellent People Skills.ask: Who would you still call if they lost their position?

Significance|Future Focused.recognize: You are aiming at a version of your life some years out that is larger than this one, and that pull is what gets you through unglamorous stretches. The cost is that the future keeps receiving all the credit, so nothing you have already done ever gets counted.
Significance|Future Focused.ask: Which of your past wins never got counted?

Significance|Generous.recognize: You give substantially, and giving is one of the ways you want your life to register, which makes you more generous than somebody giving quietly would be. The gap is that gifts with your name attached are easier to keep making than the ones without.
Significance|Generous.ask: What is the largest thing you have given anonymously?

Significance|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You can make real things with your hands and you want them to outlast you, which is why what you produce is made properly rather than quickly. The risk is that permanence and importance get confused, and you will overinvest in an object because it will still be here.
Significance|Good Practical Skills.ask: What are you making that only needs to last a year?

Significance|Good at Connecting with Oth.recognize: You link people together and your name travels with the connection, so your circle compounds faster than most people's. The cost is that a network assembled partly for standing has to be maintained, and maintenance looks identical to friendship from outside.
Significance|Good at Connecting with Oth.ask: Which of your friendships would survive being useless to you?

Significance|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You are warm and generous with credit while still wanting a great deal for yourself, and most people never manage both at once. The gap is that giving credit away can also be a way of being seen to give it, and you will know which times were which.
Significance|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: Whose achievement did you let stand entirely on its own?

Significance|Grounded.recognize: You want to matter and you are steady enough not to chase it, so your ambition has not made you erratic the way it makes other people. The risk is that steadiness looks like contentment from outside, and nobody offers you the larger thing because they assume you are already satisfied.
Significance|Grounded.ask: Who has never been told what you want?

Significance|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You get involved directly rather than directing from a distance, so your standing comes from work people watched you do. The cost is that visible work and important work are not the same set, and you will drift toward whichever one is more visible.
Significance|Hands-on and Observant.ask: What important work are you avoiding because nobody would see it?

Significance|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You find a way to make a large thing happen on resources that should not have been enough, and that is what makes your ambition credible to others. The gap is that a structure assembled out of workarounds cannot bear the scale you are aiming for, and it fails at the moment people are watching.
Significance|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What would break first if this suddenly got big?

Significance|Hardworking.recognize: You put in more hours than almost anyone and the work is genuinely good, so recognition when it comes is earned rather than engineered. The risk is that recognition is not proportional to hours, and you have no plan for the years where the two do not match.
Significance|Hardworking.ask: How long can you do this without being noticed?

Significance|Honest.recognize: You own your failures out loud, which is rare in someone who cares this much about how they are regarded. The gap is that a well-told failure builds a reputation too, and you have learned which ones are safe to tell.
Significance|Honest.ask: Which of your failures have you never told anyone?

Significance|Honest and Direct.recognize: You say hard things in public because you want to be the kind of person who does, and that motive still produces the courage. The cost is that an audience changes what gets said, and the private version of the conversation might have been more useful to them.
Significance|Honest and Direct.ask: Would you have said it that way one to one?

Significance|Idealistic.recognize: You want to matter and you want it to be for something genuinely worth mattering for, which keeps your ambition pointed at real problems. The risk is that a cause is also a platform, and you cannot always tell which part of your devotion belongs to which.
Significance|Idealistic.ask: Would you still be in this cause if you had no role in it?

Significance|Imaginative.recognize: You can see the large version of a thing before it exists, and that vision is what draws people and money toward it. The gap is that a vivid future accomplishment is satisfying on its own, and imagining it competes directly with doing it.
Significance|Imaginative.ask: How much time do you spend imagining this finished?

Significance|Independent.recognize: You want a large impact and you want it to be recognizably yours, so you will work alone rather than share the origin of something. The cost is that a thing made alone stays the size one person can make it, and the scale you want requires other people's names on it.
Significance|Independent.ask: What is too big for you to do by yourself?

Significance|Informed.recognize: You follow what is happening in your field closely, including who is rising, so you always know where the room's regard is sitting. The gap is that noting who is ascending becomes a background habit, and it quietly reframes peers as a field.
Significance|Informed.ask: Who have you started measuring yourself against?

Significance|Insightful.recognize: You see through to what a situation is really about, and being the person who names it is a large part of what you want. The risk is that the insight has to be said aloud to do that work for you, and some of them would have served better unsaid.
Significance|Insightful.ask: What did you say out loud that would have been more useful kept?

Significance|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You lift people and you want to be remembered as somebody who did, which makes your encouragement both genuine and sustained. The gap is that a legacy of raising people requires people who were raised, and there is quiet pressure on them to become your evidence.
Significance|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Who has let you down by not going as far as you expected?

Significance|Knowledgeable.recognize: You have real depth in your field and you want that depth acknowledged, so you go past where somebody satisfied with competence would stop. The cost is that expertise pursued for standing needs an audience able to appreciate it, and you gravitate toward the rooms that can.
Significance|Knowledgeable.ask: When did you last work somewhere nobody could tell how good you are?

Significance|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.recognize: You will remain with a person or an institution for the long haul, and part of what you want is for that constancy to be what you are known for. The risk is that leaving would cost you the story, and a story can outlive the reason it was true.
Significance|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.ask: Are you still here because of them, or because of what leaving would say?

Significance|Observant.recognize: You take in a room accurately, including where you sit in it, so your read of a situation carries information most people miss entirely. The gap is that constantly locating yourself in the room is tiring, and it never quite switches off.
Significance|Observant.ask: When were you last somewhere without noticing your place in it?

Significance|Open-Minded.recognize: You will take on ideas from anywhere, including ones that would reshape what you are doing, which keeps your ambition from hardening into something narrow. The cost is that a large goal held loosely can be quietly replaced by a larger one, and you have not finished any of them.
Significance|Open-Minded.ask: What have you left behind because something bigger appeared?

Significance|Organized and Effective.recognize: You run your life in a way that could handle something much larger than what you currently have, so you are prepared before the opportunity arrives. The gap is that preparation maintained for years without the opportunity turns into rehearsal, and rehearsal is comfortable.
Significance|Organized and Effective.ask: Is this preparation, or is it rehearsal?

Significance|Original.recognize: You want to be known for something nobody else could have made, which takes you past the obvious version every time. The cost is that originality and importance are separate things, and the most useful thing available to you might be an ordinary one done properly.
Significance|Original.ask: What ordinary work would help most right now?

Significance|Passionate.recognize: You care enormously and you want that caring to amount to something, so your intensity has a direction that other people's often lacks. The risk is that a cause carrying your need to matter becomes impossible to set down, and stepping away would feel like becoming nobody.
Significance|Passionate.ask: Who would you be if you were not doing this?

Significance|Perceptive.recognize: You sense how you are landing on people with unusual accuracy, which lets you adjust before a room turns on you. The gap is that a person who can always tell how they are perceived will always be checking, and you cannot switch the instrument off.
Significance|Perceptive.ask: When did you last stop wondering what somebody thought of you?

Significance|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You bring energy to a big goal and people rise toward it, so what you are part of tends to get more ambitious than it started. The cost is that your optimism is partly a need for this to be important, and a sober assessment can feel like an attack on you.
Significance|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: How do you take it when somebody says this is smaller than you think?

Significance|Principled.recognize: You want to matter and you have decided it only counts if it is done rightly, which rules out most of the shortcuts available to ambitious people. The risk is that being the principled one is itself a distinction, and a distinction can be defended for its own sake.
Significance|Principled.ask: Is that a conviction, or is it your reputation?

Significance|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You put yourself forward before being invited, which is why you are in things that other equally qualified people are not. The cost is that the habit does not distinguish between opportunities worth having and opportunities that were merely available.
Significance|Proactive Initiative.ask: What are you in right now that you never actually wanted?

Significance|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You are fast on your feet and you use it in the moments that count, so people's impression of you gets formed at your best. The gap is that quickness rewarded in public becomes a performance habit, and you start choosing the rooms where it shows.
Significance|Quick Thinkers.ask: Where do you do your slowest thinking?

Significance|Rational.recognize: You can make a rigorous case for the large thing you want to do, which is why serious people take your ambition seriously. The risk is that the case got built after the wanting, and a sound argument for something you already chose is indistinguishable from a sound argument.
Significance|Rational.ask: Did you want this before or after you could justify it?

Significance|Rational and Practical.recognize: You aim at problems that genuinely need fixing rather than ones that merely look impressive, so your ambition produces actual value. The gap is that you still need the fixing to be seen, and an unnoticed repair costs you something a purely practical person would not feel.
Significance|Rational and Practical.ask: What have you fixed that nobody ever knew was broken?

Significance|Receptive.recognize: You are willing to be shaped by what people tell you, which is unusual in someone with ambition this size and keeps you from becoming insufferable. The cost is that praise shapes you as readily as criticism does, and you cannot always tell which one is moving you.

Significance|Reliable.recognize: You do what you say, and being known as that person is part of what you are after, which makes the follow-through durable rather than situational. The gap is that a promise you cannot exit without damaging the reputation is a promise you will honor long past its usefulness.
Significance|Reliable.ask: What are you seeing through only because quitting would look bad?

Significance|Research-Oriented.recognize: You do the work to make sure your claims hold, because you understand that a large claim gets examined far more closely than a small one. The risk is that the coming examination is the reason for the rigor, and questions nobody would ever ask go unexplored.
Significance|Research-Oriented.ask: What have you not looked into because no one would challenge it?

Significance|Results Oriented.recognize: You get things over the line, and you want the line to be somewhere that matters, so what you complete tends to be worth completing. The cost is that a result nobody will notice is hard for you to stay with, and some of those were the ones that mattered most.
Significance|Results Oriented.ask: What did you abandon because the result would have been invisible?

Significance|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You are genuinely kind toward people while also wanting a great deal for yourself, and the kindness is not a strategy even though it helps you. The gap is that you cannot always tell that from inside, and the uncertainty makes you doubt your own good intentions.
Significance|Sensitive and Warm.ask: When did you last question your own motives for being good to somebody?

Significance|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You are careful about how your ambition lands on other people, so you carry it without making everyone around you feel small by comparison. The cost is that managing that impression takes constant work, and you have never let anyone see the full size of what you want.
Significance|Sensitive to Others.ask: Who has seen how much you actually want?

Significance|Sociable.recognize: You are around people constantly and it is partly how you gauge where you sit, so you always have a live sense of your position. The risk is that a social life doubling as a measuring instrument never becomes restful, and you leave gatherings tired for reasons you cannot name.
Significance|Sociable.ask: When were you last with people and not gauging anything?

Significance|Spontaneous.recognize: You will grab the chance the moment it appears, which is why the big openings in your life came from being willing to say yes fast. The gap is that a fast yes to something prominent is not the same as a considered yes, and you have said both without noticing the difference.
Significance|Spontaneous.ask: Which of your yeses was actually about the size of the thing?

Significance|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You can take on a large load and be seen doing it, and the capacity is real rather than performed. The cost is that being the one who can take anything on means the load only grows, and the reputation you built is now what sets your limits.
Significance|Strong Practical Skills.ask: What would you have to put down to find out what you actually want?

Significance|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take on more than your share and you want that to be recognized, which is an honest combination most people hide. The gap is that duty acknowledged becomes duty expected, and you cannot lighten the load now without it looking like a retreat.
Significance|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: What could you stop doing if nobody would notice you had stopped?

Significance|Strong-willed.recognize: You are determined and you are aiming at something large, so you will not be talked down to a more comfortable size. The risk is that persistence tied to being seen as important cannot tell the difference between a worthy fight and a public one.
Significance|Strong-willed.ask: Which battle are you in because it is right, and which because it is visible?

Significance|Supportive.recognize: You get behind other people's ambitions as well as your own, and you are generous about it in a way ambitious people usually are not. The cost is that helping someone rise is also proximity to the rising, and you may not know which of those drew you.
Significance|Supportive.ask: Would you help them if it made you invisible?

Significance|Very Loyal.recognize: You are committed to your people and you want that commitment to be part of what you are known for, which makes it unusually durable. The gap is that loyalty performed and loyalty felt look identical from outside, and after enough years you may not be able to separate them either.
Significance|Very Loyal.ask: Would you have stayed if nobody knew you had?

Significance|Very Responsible.recognize: You take on the big obligations and you want them, because carrying something consequential is how you know your life counts for something. The cost is that the load has to keep growing for that feeling to hold, and there is no size at which you would feel done.
Significance|Very Responsible.ask: How large would this have to be before you could rest?

Woo|Altruistic.recognize: You win people over and then actually help them, so the warmth you open with turns out to be backed by something. The cost is that you meet more people than you can carry, and the ones who needed you most are competing with everyone else you met this month.
Woo|Altruistic.ask: Who asked you for something you never got back to?

Woo|Analytical.recognize: You can win a room and also say exactly why it worked, which makes your ease with people a repeatable skill rather than a mood. The gap is that studying the mechanics of connection makes it harder to be inside one, and you can find yourself observing a friendship.
Woo|Analytical.ask: Which relationship are you watching rather than in?

Woo|Bold.recognize: You will start a conversation with anyone, at any level, without the hesitation that keeps other people in their seats. The cost is that boldness plus ease means you rarely feel the risk in an approach, so you also never register when somebody would rather not be approached.
Woo|Bold.ask: Who has been polite to you when they wanted to be left alone?

Woo|Calm and Practical.recognize: You put people at ease quickly and nothing about you seems to be trying, which is why strangers relax around you inside a minute. The gap is that the same steadiness keeps a connection at whatever temperature you set it, and you rarely let anyone see you rattled.
Woo|Calm and Practical.ask: Who has ever seen you shaken?

Woo|Charismatic.recognize: You pull people toward you and you enjoy the pulling, both instincts pointing the same direction, so a room reorganizes itself around you without your doing anything deliberate. What is missing is anything that slows a meeting down. Nothing in you asks whether this person should be let close.
Woo|Charismatic.ask: How does anyone get vetted before they are inside?

Woo|Charming.recognize: You put people at rest and you win them over, which is the same gift arriving twice, so almost nobody resists you on a first meeting. What is absent is friction of any kind, and friction is how a person finds out whether they actually like someone or were simply enjoying themselves.
Woo|Charming.ask: Who likes you, as opposed to liking being around you?

Woo|Clear Communication.recognize: You make contact and then say something worth hearing, so people leave with more than a good feeling about you. The cost is that a warm, simple version of yourself is the one meeting everybody, and anything complicated has to wait for a second conversation that often does not come.
Woo|Clear Communication.ask: Who only knows the short version of you?

Woo|Creative.recognize: You can make an introduction feel like an event, and people remember meeting you years afterward because of how you did it. The gap is that a memorable first encounter sets an expectation, and you may not want to be that person every time you see them.
Woo|Creative.ask: Who expects a version of you that is tiring to produce?

Woo|Curious.recognize: You ask people about themselves and you actually want the answer, which is why strangers tell you things very quickly. The cost is that curiosity satisfied is curiosity finished, and once you have someone's story the pull toward them can quietly fade.
Woo|Curious.ask: Who stopped being interesting once you knew their story?

Woo|Decisive Action.recognize: You decide somebody is worth knowing and you act on it at once, so your circle grew faster than that of anyone you came up with. The risk is that a fast yes to a person is still a yes, and you now have obligations to people you assessed in four minutes.
Woo|Decisive Action.ask: Which of your obligations came from a four-minute judgment?

Woo|Dedicated.recognize: You keep showing up for people long after the first meeting, which is genuinely rare in somebody who meets this many. The gap is that loyalty spread across a very wide circle is thin everywhere, and the people closest to you get the same portion as the ones you met last spring.
Woo|Dedicated.ask: Does anyone get more of you than the rest?

Woo|Determined.recognize: You will keep working on a person who has not warmed to you yet, and you usually get there in the end. The cost is that persistence aimed at winning somebody over cannot distinguish between a person who is slow and a person who has quietly declined.
Woo|Determined.ask: Who has said no to you in a way you did not hear?

Woo|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You remember the small things people mention and you bring them up later, which makes a light acquaintance feel like a real one. The gap is that recall is not intimacy, and somebody can feel deeply known by you while you know almost nothing about them.
Woo|Diligent and Observant.ask: Who thinks you are close because you remember their details?

Woo|Direct.recognize: You win people over and then tell them the truth, a combination that lets you say hard things nobody else could get away with saying. The cost is that goodwill built quickly gets spent quickly, and you may be running down an account you have not been adding to.
Woo|Direct.ask: Whose goodwill toward you have you been spending?

Woo|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You open up early, and that openness is what makes people trust you within minutes rather than months. The gap is that what you share early is the material you are comfortable sharing, and it can work as a wall that looks exactly like a door.
Woo|Direct and Authentic.ask: What do you tell everyone that stops them asking anything else?

Woo|Direct and Honest.recognize: You say the frank thing and you are liked enough to survive having said it, so you end up being the one who names what everybody was avoiding. The cost is that being liked is doing some of the work, and you have never had to test whether the point would stand on its own.
Woo|Direct and Honest.ask: Would that have landed from somebody they did not like?

Woo|Disciplined.recognize: You keep up with people by system rather than by sentiment, so nobody in your circle goes a year without hearing from you. The gap is that a scheduled relationship and a living one feel different from the other side, and people can sense when they are on a rotation.
Woo|Disciplined.ask: Who is on your list rather than on your mind?

Woo|Easygoing.recognize: You meet people effortlessly and you never seem to need anything from them, which is exactly why they come back. The cost is that a connection requiring no work also gets none, and the friendships in your life have all been left to find their own level.
Woo|Easygoing.ask: Which friendship would have gone deeper if you had worked at it?

Woo|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You can meet a great many people without it consuming your week, because you worked out long ago how to make contact quickly and move along. The gap is that speed applied to people shapes the encounter around your calendar, and depth is the first thing to go.
Woo|Efficient Organizer.ask: Does anyone get more than the time you allotted?

Woo|Empathetic.recognize: You read what somebody needs in the first minute and you give it to them, which is why people open up to you faster than they meant to. The cost is that you can produce the feeling of being understood without having done any of the work of understanding a person.
Woo|Empathetic.ask: Who felt understood by you when you had not understood them?

Woo|Energetic.recognize: You bring life into a room and you can keep doing it across a whole evening, so nobody is left standing alone where you are. The gap is that the energy going outward is not coming back in, and you can be surrounded by people and still not be met by any of them.
Woo|Energetic.ask: Who fills you up rather than taking from you?

Woo|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You keep your contacts and your commitments in good order, so the sheer number of people you know never collapses into chaos. The risk is that a person filed correctly is a person handled, and handling is not the same as caring about somebody.
Woo|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: Who has become an entry rather than a friend?

Woo|Enthusiastic.recognize: You are genuinely delighted to meet people and it shows, which is why your welcome never reads as technique. The cost is that the same delight goes to everyone, so nobody can tell from your warmth whether they matter to you or not.
Woo|Enthusiastic.ask: How would somebody know they are more to you than a stranger?

Woo|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You produce ideas and you know exactly who to call about each one, so possibilities turn into conversations fast. The gap is that a person contacted about an idea is being contacted for a reason, and you may have taught your circle that hearing from you means you want something.
Woo|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: When did you last call someone with nothing to ask for?

Woo|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You meet people easily and you are good once you have them, so a first encounter with you goes somewhere rather than stalling at pleasantries. The gap is that somebody who talks well and meets this many gets very little practice at listening for a long time.
Woo|Excellent Communicators.ask: When did you last let someone talk for ten minutes?

Woo|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You gather people and then actually put them to work, which is why your gatherings produce things instead of merely being pleasant. The cost is that a person recruited into a role has been assigned one, and some of them came for you rather than for the job.
Woo|Excellent Organizers.ask: Who joined for you and got handed a task?

Woo|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You are at ease with people and you win them over, the same instinct twice, so social situations that cost other people effort cost you nothing at all. What is absent is any signal telling you when to stop. Neither half tires of new faces, so your circle grows past what one life can hold.
Woo|Excellent People Skills.ask: How many people are you actually able to keep?

Woo|Future Focused.recognize: You meet the people you will need before you need them, which is why opportunities seem to find you rather than the other way round. The gap is that a relationship begun with a future use in mind carries that origin, and the other person may work it out before you do.
Woo|Future Focused.ask: Who did you meet because of what they might become?

Woo|Generous.recognize: You give freely to people you barely know, and that generosity is what turns an acquaintance into something warmer very fast. The cost is that giving at that rate across that many people cannot hold, and the pullback gets felt as coldness rather than as a limit.
Woo|Generous.ask: Who experienced your limit as rejection?

Woo|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You are handy and you are liked, so you are the one others call when something needs doing, and you enjoy being that person. The gap is that being useful is a dependable way to be wanted, and you may not know whether you get called for your company or your hands.
Woo|Good Practical Skills.ask: Would they still call if you could not fix anything?

Woo|Good at Connecting with Others.recognize: You meet people and you put them together, which is the same instinct pointed outward, so what you have is a network rather than a list. What is missing is any pull toward depth. Both halves reward a new contact, and neither rewards the fifth conversation with the same person.
Woo|Good at Connecting with Others.ask: Who have you had a fifth conversation with?

Woo|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You are warm and easy and people feel better for having run into you, which is a real thing to be able to hand a stranger. The cost is that somebody who is always pleasant gives away no information, and the people close to you cannot tell a good day from a bad one.
Woo|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: Who can tell when you are struggling?

Woo|Grounded.recognize: You meet a great many people and you do not lose yourself in any of them, so your ease is not the same thing as needing to be liked. The gap is that steadiness plus wide contact means you can be enormously well known and still unreached by anybody.
Woo|Grounded.ask: Who has actually gotten through to you?

Woo|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You notice the person standing alone and you are already walking over, without the internal debate that keeps other people in their chairs. The cost is that moving on a first read means you approach people according to how they look, and some of them were fine.
Woo|Hands-on and Observant.ask: Does everyone standing alone want company?

Woo|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You can find your way into any room through somebody you know, and if you do not know somebody you will inside the hour. The gap is that access gained through people has to be repaid in people, and you carry favors you have never counted.
Woo|Handy and Resourceful.ask: Who is owed something by you right now?

Woo|Hardworking.recognize: You put real work into your relationships, which is why the number of people who would take your call is far larger than it has any right to be. The cost is that keeping up that many takes hours nobody sees, and it is labor you have never let yourself count as labor.
Woo|Hardworking.ask: How many hours a week go to keeping up with people?

Woo|Honest.recognize: You are open about yourself early and people respond to it, so trust arrives faster with you than with almost anyone else. The gap is that fast trust is not tested trust, and somebody can give you a great deal before they have any evidence that they should.
Woo|Honest.ask: Who trusted you before you had earned it?

Woo|Honest and Direct.recognize: You are liked and you are blunt, so you can tell somebody something difficult in the same meeting where you met them. The cost is that the warmth carries the bluntness, and you never find out which of your hard words were actually taken in.
Woo|Honest and Direct.ask: Was it taken in, or were you simply forgiven for saying it?

Woo|Idealistic.recognize: You believe in people on first meeting, and that belief is often exactly what brings out the version you thought you saw. The gap is that a first impression carrying that much hope has a long way to fall, and you are quietly disillusioned more often than you let on.
Woo|Idealistic.ask: Who has let you down that you never told?

Woo|Imaginative.recognize: You can see what a person might become and you talk to them as though they already are, which is why people find you unusually encouraging to be near. The cost is that the person you are speaking to is not the one in front of you, and they can feel the difference.
Woo|Imaginative.ask: Who are you talking to when you talk to them?

Woo|Independent.recognize: You know an enormous number of people and you need none of them, which keeps your warmth clean of neediness. The gap is that never needing anyone means never asking, and a circle that has never been asked for anything does not know it is allowed to give.
Woo|Independent.ask: Who is allowed to be necessary to you?

Woo|Informed.recognize: You know what everyone is doing and you follow their news, which makes you the person others check with to find out about somebody else. The cost is that knowing about a person feels like knowing them, and you can carry an outdated picture of someone for years.
Woo|Informed.ask: Who do you know about rather than know?

Woo|Insightful.recognize: You get a person quickly and you can say something true about them within minutes, which is why first conversations with you go deep fast. The gap is that a fast accurate read means you rarely stay long enough to be surprised, and people are mostly surprising later.
Woo|Insightful.ask: Who turned out different from your first read of them?

Woo|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You make people feel good about themselves on very little acquaintance, and you mean it, which is the only reason it works. The cost is that encouragement given this freely is impossible to calibrate, and the person who needed a harder word got the same warmth as everybody else.
Woo|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Is your encouragement calibrated to anything?

Woo|Knowledgeable.recognize: You have something worth hearing in most conversations, so meeting you is useful as well as pleasant. The gap is that being interesting is a way of holding the floor, and a person who is always contributing is not always taking anything in.
Woo|Knowledgeable.ask: What did you learn from the last person you met?

Woo|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.recognize: You hold onto people, so the friends you made twenty years ago are still friends, which is rare in somebody who keeps meeting new ones. The cost is that a circle that only ever grows takes more time each year, and the oldest relationships get the least of it.
Woo|Loyal, Patient, and Reliable.ask: Which of your oldest friends have you let slide?

Woo|Observant.recognize: You read a room before you walk into it and you know who to approach, so your warmth arrives where it will actually land. The gap is that choosing well means you are always choosing, and the person you consistently pass over never learns why.
Woo|Observant.ask: Who do you keep not approaching?

Woo|Open-Minded.recognize: You will get on with anyone regardless of where they came from, which is why your circle looks nothing like a single tribe. The cost is that being at home with everyone can mean belonging fully to nobody, and you may have no group that would notice your absence.
Woo|Open-Minded.ask: Which group would notice if you stopped coming?

Woo|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have a way of keeping track of everybody, so the size of your circle never turns into a mess. The gap is that a person managed by a system receives what the system allows, and nobody in your system gets the unplanned hour that friendships are actually made of.
Woo|Organized and Effective.ask: Who last got an unplanned hour from you?

Woo|Original.recognize: You are memorable because you do not meet people the way everyone else does, so an encounter with you does not blur into the others they had that day. The cost is that being distinctive is its own reward, and you may be more interested in the impression than in the person receiving it.
Woo|Original.ask: Do you want to meet them, or to be met by them?

Woo|Passionate.recognize: You meet people with real heat and they feel chosen, which is why a first conversation with you can change somebody's week. The gap is that intensity offered that widely cannot be sustained, and the person you were fervent about in March may not hear from you in June.
Woo|Passionate.ask: Who got your whole attention once and never again?

Woo|Perceptive.recognize: You sense how somebody wants to be met and you meet them that way, which is why you almost never misjudge an opening. The cost is that adjusting to each person means there is a version of you for everyone, and nobody has met whoever is underneath all of them.
Woo|Perceptive.ask: Which version of you is the actual one?

Woo|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You lift a room simply by arriving in it, and people organize their evening around whether you are coming. The gap is that somebody expected to lift the room cannot arrive heavy, and you have been performing brightness on nights when you did not have any.
Woo|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: When did you last show up in the state you were actually in?

Woo|Principled.recognize: You are warm with everyone but you will not be bought by anybody, so your friendliness has never cost you your judgment. The cost is that a person who likes you assumes they also have your approval, and the correction lands far harder for having been a surprise.
Woo|Principled.ask: Who assumed your warmth meant agreement?

Woo|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You go over and say hello before anyone else has finished deciding whether to, so you are the reason a group of strangers becomes a room. The gap is that initiating constantly means you set the opening terms of every relationship, and you have rarely been the one approached.
Woo|Proactive Initiative.ask: Who has ever come to you first?

Woo|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You are fast in conversation and it makes you a pleasure to talk to, so people leave feeling sharper than they arrived. The cost is that quickness fills silences, and silence is where the person you are with would have said the real thing.
Woo|Quick Thinkers.ask: What did somebody nearly tell you before you filled the pause?

Woo|Rational.recognize: You are liked and you argue well, so people accept your position and also feel good about having accepted it. The gap is that agreement given warmly is not the same as agreement given after thought, and you cannot tell the two apart from where you are sitting.
Woo|Rational.ask: Who agreed with you because they liked you?

Woo|Rational and Practical.recognize: You make yourself handy early in a relationship, so people have a reason to keep you around before they have any attachment to you. The cost is that being of use, offered up front, becomes the basis, and you may not believe anybody stays for anything else.
Woo|Rational and Practical.ask: Would anyone keep you around if you were no help at all?

Woo|Receptive.recognize: You are easy to approach and you let people in without a vetting period, which is why so many relationships in the world start with you. The gap is that a door that is always unlocked cannot signal anything, and the person you truly want near you cannot tell they were chosen.
Woo|Receptive.ask: How would somebody know you picked them?

Woo|Reliable.recognize: You are liked and you follow through, a combination rarer than either half alone, so your friendliness comes backed by evidence. The cost is that the number of people counting on you grew alongside the number you met, and those two lines were never meant to match.
Woo|Reliable.ask: Is that number larger than you can actually serve?

Woo|Research-Oriented.recognize: You find out about people before you meet them, so you arrive already knowing what matters to them and the conversation starts warm. The gap is that preparation of that kind is indistinguishable from technique, and if they ever notice it, everything genuine about you gets read again.
Woo|Research-Oriented.ask: How would they feel about how much you knew before you met?

Woo|Results Oriented.recognize: You meet people and something comes of it, so your relationships produce rather than merely continue. The cost is that a friendship with no result attached has nothing holding it in your calendar, and those are the ones that quietly lapse.
Woo|Results Oriented.ask: Which friendship lapsed because it was not going anywhere?

Woo|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You meet people with genuine care rather than technique, and they can tell the difference inside a sentence. The gap is that caring quickly about a great many people is still caring, and the accumulated weight of that many attachments is something you carry entirely alone.
Woo|Sensitive and Warm.ask: Who do you worry about that has no idea you do?

Woo|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You notice when somebody is uncomfortable and you fix it before they have to say anything, which is why people feel safe near you so early. The cost is that smoothing every encounter turns a pleasure into labor, and you go home tired from a party you enjoyed.
Woo|Sensitive to Others.ask: When were you last at a gathering without managing it?

Woo|Sociable.recognize: You seek people out and you win them once you have them, the same appetite twice over, so you are almost never alone and almost never a stranger. What is missing is any counterweight pulling you inward. Nothing in the pairing wants a quiet evening, so you have not had one in years.
Woo|Sociable.ask: Does a quiet evening sound restful or unbearable?

Woo|Spontaneous.recognize: You will talk to whoever is in front of you and go wherever the evening leads, so your best relationships came out of nights you did not plan. The gap is that the same openness means the friend you meant to ring is still unrung, because somebody nearer always turned up.
Woo|Spontaneous.ask: Which name keeps moving down the list?

Woo|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You can take on almost anything practical and you are liked, so people bring you both their problems and their evenings. The cost is that being the one who can manage it and the one who is good company means you get asked for constantly, from two different directions.
Woo|Strong Practical Skills.ask: Which kind of asking wears you out more?

Woo|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take your responsibilities to people seriously, so an acquaintance of yours gets treated as a commitment rather than a contact. The gap is that duty scaled across a very large circle becomes a load, and you cannot set any single piece of it down without it looking personal.
Woo|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: Which of these would you drop if it would hurt nobody?

Woo|Strong-willed.recognize: You are warm and you are immovable, so people who assumed your friendliness meant pliability find out otherwise eventually. The cost is that the discovery is jarring, and a person can feel misled by something you never actually claimed.
Woo|Strong-willed.ask: Who felt misled by your firmness?

Woo|Supportive.recognize: You get behind people early, often before they have shown you much, and that early belief is worth more to them than the later kind. The gap is that support given at the start of an acquaintance rests on very little, and you will occasionally have championed the wrong person in public.
Woo|Supportive.ask: Who did you vouch for too soon?

Woo|Very Loyal.recognize: You are loyal to everybody you have taken on, and you have taken on a great many, so almost nobody in your life has ever been dropped. The cost is that loyalty at that volume cannot be deep in every case, and people who assume they have all of your commitment have part of it.
Woo|Very Loyal.ask: Is your loyalty as deep as people assume it is?

Woo|Very Responsible.recognize: You take ownership of how the people around you are doing, which is why yours is a circle rather than a contact list. The gap is that responsibility for that many is not something a person can actually discharge, and you carry a low steady failure nobody would ever charge you with.
Woo|Very Responsible.ask: Who are you quietly failing in your own accounting?

Adaptability|Altruistic.recognize: You are available to whoever needs you right now, without your day having had to anticipate them, so help from you arrives at the moment it is wanted. The cost is that a life organized around other people's immediate needs has no room held back for your own, and none ever gets added.
Adaptability|Altruistic.ask: What did you set aside for yourself this week?

Adaptability|Analytical.recognize: You take in a situation as it actually is rather than as your plan expected it to be, so your read stays accurate while other people defend a forecast. The gap is that responding to what is in front of you means you rarely step back far enough to see the shape across months.
Adaptability|Analytical.ask: What have you been too close to notice?

Adaptability|Bold.recognize: You go where the moment takes you and you are not frightened by not knowing what is next, which is why you have lived more than most people your age. The cost is that boldness plus openness leaves nothing anchoring you, and you can be far from where you meant to be before anyone notices.
Adaptability|Bold.ask: Where did you mean to be by now?

Adaptability|Calm and Practical.recognize: You take whatever the day brings without a ripple, so a chaotic situation around you gets handled rather than dramatized. The gap is that being unflappable plus willing to go along means you absorb changes that somebody should have been made to justify.
Adaptability|Calm and Practical.ask: What change did you accept that nobody had to explain?

Adaptability|Charismatic.recognize: You are compelling in the moment and you need no script, so you are at your best in exactly the situations that undo well-prepared people. The cost is that improvised brilliance is hard to repeat on demand, and you may have built a reputation you cannot deliver on a scheduled Tuesday.
Adaptability|Charismatic.ask: What do you owe people that requires planning?

Adaptability|Charming.recognize: You handle whatever arrives and you make it pleasant while you do it, so difficulty around you turns into an anecdote rather than a crisis. The gap is that smoothing a problem in the moment can keep it from being properly named, and it will arrive again in the same shape.
Adaptability|Charming.ask: What keeps coming back that you keep handling?

Adaptability|Clear Communication.recognize: You can explain what is happening right now in terms anyone can act on, which is why people look to you the moment a plan collapses. The cost is that you speak fluently about today and vaguely about next quarter, and some rooms need the second thing more.
Adaptability|Clear Communication.ask: What have you not said about where this is going?

Adaptability|Creative.recognize: You make things in response to what is in front of you rather than to a brief, so your work has a liveness that planned work often lacks entirely. The gap is that responsive work is scattered work, and you have many good beginnings and very few finished pieces.
Adaptability|Creative.ask: How many unfinished pieces are there?

Adaptability|Curious.recognize: You follow whatever is interesting right now, so you have picked up an enormous range of things nobody ever assigned you. The cost is that a mind going wherever the moment points accumulates breadth without depth, and you may be a beginner in twenty things at once.
Adaptability|Curious.ask: What are you actually expert in?

Adaptability|Decisive Action.recognize: You read the moment and act inside it, so you are decisive without being rigid, which is a genuinely rare pairing. The gap is that choices made this way are optimized for now, and a run of good immediate calls can add up to a direction you never chose.
Adaptability|Decisive Action.ask: Did you choose this direction or arrive at it?

Adaptability|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with people and commitments while staying loose about how, so your loyalty survives circumstances that break more rigid versions of it. The cost is that looseness about the how can quietly become looseness about the what, and you may be honoring something that changed underneath you.
Adaptability|Dedicated.ask: Is this still the thing you signed up for?

Adaptability|Determined.recognize: You keep going and you change shape in order to do it, so obstacles that stop other people simply reroute you instead. The gap is that somebody who never stops and never insists on a route can travel enormous distances without arriving anywhere in particular.
Adaptability|Determined.ask: Where is all of this effort taking you?

Adaptability|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You spot what is changing while it is still small, because you are watching what is actually happening rather than checking against a plan. The cost is that constant adjustment to small shifts means you are always altering course, and the people around you experience that as instability.

Adaptability|Direct.recognize: You say what the situation calls for at the moment it calls for it, so very little festers around you. The gap is that a remark shaped entirely by the moment can contradict one you made last week, and people cannot work out what your actual position is.
Adaptability|Direct.ask: What do you consistently believe about this?

Adaptability|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You are whoever you actually are in the moment, without managing the continuity between versions, which is why you seem unusually free to people. The cost is that others need continuity in order to trust somebody, and they can experience your honesty as unreliability.
Adaptability|Direct and Authentic.ask: Who cannot predict which you they will get?

Adaptability|Direct and Honest.recognize: You will say the true thing as the situation develops rather than saving it for a better time, so information moves fast around you. The gap is that honesty without timing is honesty delivered whenever it occurred to you, and the same words land very differently an hour later.
Adaptability|Direct and Honest.ask: Is timing something you think about at all?

Adaptability|Disciplined.recognize: You hold a few habits fixed and let everything else move, which gives you a stable base without a rigid life. The cost is that those habits were chosen long ago and are the one part of you that never responds to anything, so they may be the least examined thing you do.
Adaptability|Disciplined.ask: Which of your fixed habits no longer fits your life?

Adaptability|Easygoing.recognize: You take things as they come and you are untroubled by not knowing what comes next, which is the same disposition arriving twice. What is missing is anything pulling against the current. Nothing in you objects to going along, so the question of whether you wanted this never gets raised.
Adaptability|Easygoing.ask: When did you last object to anything?

Adaptability|Efficient Organizer.recognize: You get things done in whatever order the day allows rather than the order you intended, so you stay productive under conditions that stall other people entirely. The gap is that working through whatever is available means the important slow thing never gets to the front.
Adaptability|Efficient Organizer.ask: What important thing has been waiting the longest?

Adaptability|Empathetic.recognize: You feel what is happening in a room and you move with it, so people find you unusually easy to be near when they are struggling. The cost is that responding to whoever is most in need means your own state gets set by the last person you sat with.
Adaptability|Empathetic.ask: Whose mood are you currently carrying?

Adaptability|Energetic.recognize: You have energy for whatever turns up, so an unexpected day does not empty you out the way it does people who had a plan. The gap is that energy always available to the unexpected gets entirely spent on it, and the things that needed a reserved block of hours never got one.
Adaptability|Energetic.ask: What needs a whole afternoon and has never had one?

Adaptability|Enjoy Creating Order.recognize: You bring order to whatever is in front of you without needing the whole system settled first, so messes around you shrink steadily. The cost is that order created in the moment does not persist, and you may be sorting the same things repeatedly rather than fixing why they scatter.
Adaptability|Enjoy Creating Order.ask: What keeps needing to be sorted out again?

Adaptability|Enthusiastic.recognize: You get excited about whatever is happening now, which makes you wonderful company and a real lift to a room. The gap is that excitement attached to the current thing transfers cleanly to the next one, and people who caught it from you can be left holding a project you have already left.
Adaptability|Enthusiastic.ask: What did you get people excited about and then leave?

Adaptability|Excellent Brainstormers.recognize: You produce ideas in response to what is actually in the room, so your suggestions fit the situation rather than a template you brought with you. The cost is that ideas made on the spot are tied to the spot, and almost none of them survive the walk to the car.
Adaptability|Excellent Brainstormers.ask: Which of your best ideas never got written down?

Adaptability|Excellent Communicators.recognize: You can speak to whatever is actually happening rather than delivering the remarks you brought, so a room feels addressed rather than talked at. The gap is that improvised speech leaves no record, and what you said in the moment cannot be checked later, including by you.
Adaptability|Excellent Communicators.ask: What did you promise in a room that never got written down?

Adaptability|Excellent Organizers.recognize: You can reorganize on the fly when a plan fails, so what you run bends instead of breaking. The cost is that a group whose shape keeps changing has to relearn itself constantly, and the people inside it spend energy on orientation that costs you nothing.
Adaptability|Excellent Organizers.ask: How much of your team's week goes to working out what changed?

Adaptability|Excellent People Skills.recognize: You meet people where they are on the day, so somebody having a bad week gets a different you than they got last month, and both were right. The gap is that reading each person fresh means you form few fixed expectations, and people can behave badly around you for years without it adding up.
Adaptability|Excellent People Skills.ask: Does anybody in your life have a record with you?

Adaptability|Future Focused.recognize: You can see where things are heading and you stay loose about how to get there, so your long view survives contact with a week that goes wrong. The gap is that a horizon plus total openness about the route means nothing between here and there ever actually gets scheduled.
Adaptability|Future Focused.ask: What is the next concrete step toward it?

Adaptability|Generous.recognize: You give what you have when the need appears, without waiting for a planned moment, so your generosity is unusually well timed. The cost is that giving in response to whoever is in front of you has no budget behind it, and you can be emptied out by a run of reasonable yeses.
Adaptability|Generous.ask: How many small yeses did you say this month?

Adaptability|Good Practical Skills.recognize: You can fix what has gone wrong with whatever is at hand, so a broken thing near you gets working again quickly. The gap is that responsiveness plus practical skill means you are always mending and never replacing, and the same underlying problem has now been solved fifteen times.
Adaptability|Good Practical Skills.ask: What have you repaired more than three times?

Adaptability|Good at Connecting with Oth.recognize: You meet people as they come and you put them together as the situation suggests, so your relationships are wide and lightly held. The cost is that a connection made in passing needs somebody to follow up, and following up is precisely the kind of scheduled work you avoid.
Adaptability|Good at Connecting with Oth.ask: Who did you mean to get back to and never did?

Adaptability|Good-Natured and Positive.recognize: You take what comes with good humor, so being around you makes a difficult day feel survivable to everybody else. The gap is that treating everything as workable means genuinely bad news gets the same reception as a schedule change, and nobody can tell from your face which one arrived.
Adaptability|Good-Natured and Positive.ask: What news deserved a stronger reaction from you than it got?

Adaptability|Grounded.recognize: You are settled in yourself while staying loose about circumstances, so change does not shake you the way it shakes people who need things fixed in place. The cost is that being unshaken removes the discomfort that usually tells a person a particular change was bad for them.
Adaptability|Grounded.ask: Which change was worse for you than you let yourself feel?

Adaptability|Hands-on and Observant.recognize: You see what the moment requires and your hands are already on it, so nothing sits waiting for a decision around you. The gap is that working from whatever is in front of you means the invisible problem, the one with no symptom yet, never gets touched at all.
Adaptability|Hands-on and Observant.ask: What is wrong that has not shown itself yet?

Adaptability|Handy and Resourceful.recognize: You can make something work out of whatever happens to be available, which is why constraints that stop other people barely register with you. The cost is that a life of clever momentary fixes accumulates a great many held-together things, and you are the only one who knows where they all are.
Adaptability|Handy and Resourceful.ask: What would fall apart if you were away for a month?

Adaptability|Hardworking.recognize: You will work at whatever the day puts in front of you without needing it to be the thing you planned, so your hours always go somewhere useful. The gap is that useful and important are different things, and a decade of responsive labor can leave nothing you would point at.
Adaptability|Hardworking.ask: Is there anything with your name on it after all these hours?

Adaptability|Honest.recognize: You tell people the truth as it stands today, and you will tell them a different one tomorrow if it has changed, which is more honest than most people manage. The cost is that others hear a revised position as a broken word, and you may not have realized a word was given.
Adaptability|Honest.ask: What did somebody take as a promise that you meant as a view?

Adaptability|Honest and Direct.recognize: You respond to what is actually in front of you and you say so plainly, so nothing gets managed into vagueness around you. The gap is that a plain statement about a moving situation gets quoted later as though fixed, and you will be held to a sentence you meant for one afternoon.
Adaptability|Honest and Direct.ask: Do people treat your sentences as positions?

Adaptability|Idealistic.recognize: You hold a picture of how things ought to be while staying loose about how they get there, which keeps your hope from turning brittle. The cost is that a vision with no fixed route can be deferred indefinitely, and deferral never feels like giving up.
Adaptability|Idealistic.ask: How long has this been a someday?

Adaptability|Imaginative.recognize: You invent in the moment out of a large stock of what could be, so what you come up with on the spot beats most people's prepared answer. The gap is that imagination plus responsiveness lets you be somewhere else entirely while appearing engaged, and the people with you notice more than you think.
Adaptability|Imaginative.ask: Where do you go when you are not in the conversation?

Adaptability|Independent.recognize: You go where you want when you want, and answering to nobody means no one else's plan constrains your day. The cost is that a life with no fixed obligations to other people is a life other people cannot lean on, and leaning is how most closeness gets built.
Adaptability|Independent.ask: Who could count on you for something at a fixed hour?

Adaptability|Informed.recognize: You know what is happening right now because you are watching rather than working from a briefing, so your picture is current in a way most people's is not. The gap is that a current picture with no long memory behind it means you can be surprised by something that has already happened three times.
Adaptability|Informed.ask: What has surprised you that should not have?

Adaptability|Insightful.recognize: You see straight into what a situation actually is, in the moment, with no preparation, which is why you are the useful one when something breaks unexpectedly. The cost is that insight arriving in the moment departs with it, and you rarely write down what you understood.
Adaptability|Insightful.ask: What did you understand once and then lose?

Adaptability|Kind and Encouraging.recognize: You give people what they need on the day rather than what you decided last week they would need, so your encouragement always fits. The gap is that somebody who meets you where you are will not hold you to where you said you would be, and some people needed that holding.
Adaptability|Kind and Encouraging.ask: Is meeting people where they are always the kindest thing?

Adaptability|Knowledgeable.recognize: You bring what you have learned to bear on whatever comes up, so your range gets used rather than shelved. The cost is that learning driven entirely by what happens to arise has no syllabus, and there are gaps in your field you have simply never bumped into.
Adaptability|Knowledgeable.ask: What in your field have you never had a reason to learn?

Adaptability|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.recognize: You remain with people through changing circumstances precisely because you do not need the circumstances to hold, which makes your loyalty more durable than the rigid kind. The gap is that being loyal without being predictable means people trust that you care and not that you will be there Thursday.
Adaptability|Loyal, Patient, and Reliabl.ask: Do people trust you to care, or to turn up?

Adaptability|Observant.recognize: You take in what is actually happening rather than what was supposed to, which is why you catch shifts that people working from a plan miss completely. The cost is that somebody always reading the room is somebody always available to be redirected by it.
Adaptability|Observant.ask: When did the room last change your mind for you?

Adaptability|Open-Minded.recognize: You will consider anything and you will go along with most of it, the same willingness arriving twice, so you have almost no resistance to offer a bad idea. What is absent is a position to be argued out of. Nothing in you holds a line, so agreement from you carries very little information.

Adaptability|Organized and Effective.recognize: You have enough system to function and enough give to survive a week that does not go as written, a balance most people never find. The cost is that when the two conflict the give always wins, and the parts of your setup that only work if followed exactly are the parts quietly failing.
Adaptability|Organized and Effective.ask: Which of your systems only holds when the week is calm?

Adaptability|Original.recognize: You respond to each situation on its own terms rather than reaching for the standard answer, so what you do is unlike what anybody else would have done. The gap is that originality arrived at in the moment cannot be taught to anyone, and nobody could take over from you.
Adaptability|Original.ask: Who could do what you do if you stopped?

Adaptability|Passionate.recognize: You throw yourself entirely into whatever is happening, so the thing in front of you gets all of you rather than a portion. The cost is that intensity attached to the current moment leaves the previous one behind, and people who had your whole self last month can feel the difference now.
Adaptability|Passionate.ask: Who had all of you once and can tell they no longer do?

Adaptability|Perceptive.recognize: You sense where a situation is heading and you shift with it before anyone announces anything, so you are rarely caught out. The gap is that adjusting to what you sense means acting on impressions nobody ever stated, and you can be responding to something that was not happening.
Adaptability|Perceptive.ask: When did you adjust to something that turned out not to be real?

Adaptability|Positive and Enthusiastic.recognize: You meet each turn of events with energy rather than resistance, so a group that has just lost its plan looks at you and keeps going. The cost is that optimism plus willingness means you will cheerfully absorb a change that deserved a fight.
Adaptability|Positive and Enthusiastic.ask: Does your good cheer ever cost the group a fight worth having?

Adaptability|Principled.recognize: You have fixed convictions and total openness about everything else, so your principles are not cluttered with preferences pretending to be principles. The gap is that somebody this movable on practical questions can be maneuvered into a place where the conviction is the only thing left to give up.
Adaptability|Principled.ask: How did you end up somewhere that asks this of you?

Adaptability|Proactive Initiative.recognize: You are prepared for whatever appears and you start on it at once, so an opportunity never has to wait for you to be free. The cost is that always being available to what appears means you have almost never begun something that nothing prompted.
Adaptability|Proactive Initiative.ask: What have you started that nothing prompted?

Adaptability|Quick Thinkers.recognize: You think on your feet and you are comfortable without a script, which is why an unexpected meeting is where you do your best work. The gap is that quickness in the moment gets rewarded so consistently that you have stopped preparing at all, including for the things that need it.
Adaptability|Quick Thinkers.ask: What did you walk into unprepared that deserved better?

Adaptability|Rational.recognize: You work out what makes sense given the situation as it stands now, rather than defending the thinking behind a plan that has been overtaken. The cost is that always starting from current conditions produces a run of locally sound choices that do not add up to a coherent life.
Adaptability|Rational.ask: Does the sum of your sensible choices make sense?

Adaptability|Rational and Practical.recognize: You do what will work here, with what is here, so you are exactly the person a stalled situation needs. The gap is that what works now and what works are not the same question, and you almost never get asked the second one.
Adaptability|Rational and Practical.ask: What works now that will not work in a year?

Adaptability|Receptive.recognize: You are open to what arrives and you take it in rather than pushing back, the same instinct doubled, so almost nothing gets turned away by you. What is missing is any filter at the door. Neither half evaluates before accepting, so your life is largely composed of whatever happened to come.
Adaptability|Receptive.ask: What in your life did you actually choose?

Adaptability|Reliable.recognize: You will be there, and you will work around whatever is in the way in order to be, so your promises survive circumstances that would void other people's. The cost is that being able to absorb any obstacle means nobody ever hears that something was hard, and the load you carry stays invisible.
Adaptability|Reliable.ask: What did the last thing you pulled off actually take?

Adaptability|Research-Oriented.recognize: You take in what is true now rather than relying on what you established last year, so your information does not go stale on you. The gap is that continuous updating with no settled base means you can be talked out of something well grounded by something merely recent.
Adaptability|Research-Oriented.ask: What did you abandon that was right?

Adaptability|Results Oriented.recognize: You will change the route as often as needed to arrive, so the goal survives obstacles that would have ended somebody more attached to the plan. The cost is that a goal met by constant improvisation cannot be repeated, and next time you will begin from nothing again.
Adaptability|Results Oriented.ask: What did you learn last time that you could use now?

Adaptability|Sensitive and Warm.recognize: You meet people in whatever state they are in and you are kind about it, so nobody has to be doing well in order to be around you. The gap is that meeting everyone where they are includes people who are stuck, and you can spend years being gentle with somebody who needed a push.
Adaptability|Sensitive and Warm.ask: Who needed a push and got your patience instead?

Adaptability|Sensitive to Others.recognize: You change what you are doing to fit what other people need, and you do it without being asked, the same yielding arriving twice. What is absent is anything holding your own shape. With nothing pushing back, you can be entirely rearranged by a room and not notice until you are home.
Adaptability|Sensitive to Others.ask: What did you want before you walked in there?

Adaptability|Sociable.recognize: You go where people are and you take the evening as it comes, so your social life happens rather than getting organized. The cost is that a life of turning up wherever is convenient means the friendships you have are the ones geography chose for you.
Adaptability|Sociable.ask: Which friend would you never see if it took effort?

Adaptability|Spontaneous.recognize: You act on the moment and you go with whatever the moment turns into, the same freedom twice, so you are almost never constrained by yesterday's decision. What is missing is anything carrying forward. Neither half holds a line from one day to the next, so nothing accumulates.
Adaptability|Spontaneous.ask: What in your life has accumulated?

Adaptability|Strong Practical Skills.recognize: You can take on whatever the day produces, so problems get dealt with as they surface instead of queuing up. The gap is that being able to absorb anything means nothing ever gets escalated, and the person who could have fixed the cause never finds out there was one.
Adaptability|Strong Practical Skills.ask: Who does not know how much you have absorbed?

Adaptability|Strong Sense of Duty.recognize: You take what is asked of you seriously and you rearrange yourself to meet it, so you are dependable without needing conditions to be right. The cost is that a person who can always accommodate will always be the one asked, and the asking grows to fill whatever room you give it.
Adaptability|Strong Sense of Duty.ask: What are you doing purely because you were the one who could?

Adaptability|Strong-willed.recognize: You are firm about what matters and loose about everything else, so you spend your resistance only where it counts. The gap is that giving way constantly on small things builds a habit, and by the time the important one arrives you may not recognize it as the exception.
Adaptability|Strong-willed.ask: How do you tell a small thing from a real one?

Adaptability|Supportive.recognize: You adjust to what somebody needs from you rather than offering everyone the same help, so your support actually fits the person. The cost is that help shaped entirely around the other person leaves no trace of what you think, and they may never learn you disagreed.
Adaptability|Supportive.ask: What do you think about their plan that you have never said?

Adaptability|Very Loyal.recognize: You stay with people while everything around the relationship changes, so your loyalty does not depend on conditions holding. The gap is that being able to accommodate anything means you have accommodated some things that should have ended it.
Adaptability|Very Loyal.ask: Is there anything this relationship could do that would end it?

Adaptability|Very Responsible.recognize: You take on what falls to you as the day unfolds, so responsibilities get met without anybody having to allocate them. The cost is that a duty taken up informally is a duty with no boundary, and nobody, including you, could say where yours ends.
Adaptability|Very Responsible.ask: Where does what you are responsible for actually end?

Connectedness|Altruistic.recognize: You help people because you understand yourself to be part of the same fabric they are, so your giving has no calculation anywhere in it. The cost is that somebody who sees every need as bound up with their own has no principled place to stop, and the world does not run out of need.
Connectedness|Altruistic.ask: What need have you decided is not yours?

Connectedness|Analytical.recognize: You see how the pieces relate and you can also show your working, so your sense of the whole is not merely intuition. The gap is that analysis can be used to justify something you already felt, and a rigorous case for a design does not make the design real.
Connectedness|Analytical.ask: Which of these would survive somebody else's scrutiny?

Connectedness|Bold.recognize: You act on your sense that things are meant to fit together, which lets you take steps other people would consider unfounded. The cost is that conviction about meaning plus a willingness to move means you can commit hard to a coincidence.
Connectedness|Bold.ask: What did you act on that turned out to be a coincidence?

Connectedness|Calm and Practical.recognize: You hold a wide view of how things fit and you stay practical inside it, so your sense of meaning never floats free of the actual week. The gap is that steadiness plus a belief that things work out looks identical to acceptance, and some situations needed alarm.
Connectedness|Calm and Practical.ask: What have you made peace with that should have alarmed you?

Connectedness|Charismatic.recognize: You can make people feel part of something larger, and they feel it in the room rather than merely agreeing with it afterward. The cost is that a shared sense of meaning is powerful and very hard to check, and a group can travel a long way on a feeling you gave them.
Connectedness|Charismatic.ask: What is your group believing because you believe it?

Connectedness|Charming.recognize: You take the guard down and help people see how their piece fits the whole, so belonging arrives quickly around you. The gap is that a place made for somebody easily can be a place you assigned rather than one they chose.
Connectedness|Charming.ask: Who is in a role you decided suited them?

Connectedness|Clear Communication.recognize: You can say straightforwardly how the parts relate, so what would be mysticism coming from somebody else is usable coming from you. The cost is that a clear account of a large design sounds far more certain than it is, and people take your framework as a finding.
Connectedness|Clear Communication.ask: How sure are you actually about that?

Connectedness|Creative.recognize: You make work that carries a sense of the larger whole, which is why what you produce has resonance rather than only competence. The gap is that meaning found in the making is meaning you supplied, and you may be moved by your own work in ways nobody else is.
Connectedness|Creative.ask: Does it land for other people the way it lands for you?

Connectedness|Curious.recognize: You follow the ways things relate to one another, so your questions cross fields that other people keep carefully separate. The cost is that a mind looking for how everything joins up will always find a join, and some of them are your own doing.
Connectedness|Curious.ask: What join have you made that nobody else can see?

Connectedness|Decisive Action.recognize: You act on your sense of how things are meant to go without waiting for the evidence to be complete, so you can decide in situations where it never will be. The gap is that acting fast on a felt design makes it harder to abandon, because now your choices are attached to it.
Connectedness|Decisive Action.ask: Would you still see the design if you had not moved on it?

Connectedness|Dedicated.recognize: You stay with things because you believe they belong to something that matters beyond the immediate result, and that belief carries you past ordinary discouragement. The cost is that meaning attached to a commitment makes leaving feel like a betrayal of the meaning rather than a change of plan.

Connectedness|Determined.recognize: You keep going because you understand the work as part of a larger purpose, so setbacks read as part of the story rather than as evidence against it. The gap is that a framework where every obstacle is meaningful cannot produce the signal that you ought to stop.
Connectedness|Determined.ask: What would count as a sign to stop?

Connectedness|Diligent and Observant.recognize: You notice small things and you notice what they belong to, so you register the significance of details other people record and forget. The cost is that assigning meaning to small events is a habit that does not switch off, and an ordinary coincidence can occupy you for days.
Connectedness|Diligent and Observant.ask: What small thing have you been reading into?

Connectedness|Direct.recognize: You will say plainly what you sense is going on beneath a situation, which spares people working it out alone. The gap is that a flat statement about hidden meaning is very hard to dispute, and people go along with your reading rather than argue about something that cannot be tested.
Connectedness|Direct.ask: Has anyone ever successfully disagreed with one of your readings?

Connectedness|Direct and Authentic.recognize: You talk openly about how you understand things to fit together, including the parts most people keep private. The cost is that sharing a framework this personal invites others inside it, and some of them adopt it without ever having tested it for themselves.
Connectedness|Direct and Authentic.ask: Who took on your way of seeing without questioning it?
